Gabriel, appearing as a stranger, asked the Prophet about Islam, faith, excellence and the signs of the Hour; Ibn Umar cited it against those denying Divine Decree.
Men asking what Allah requires were told prayer, Ramadan's fast, Zakat and Hajj, with Paradise if true to it, and Islam is built on five pillars.
The Abdul Qais delegation was commanded faith in Allah, explained as the testimony, prayer, Zakat, fasting and a fifth of booty, and forbidden four kinds of drinking vessels.
Sending Mu'adh to People of the Book in Yemen, the Prophet told him to call them first to the testimony, then prayer, then Zakat, without taking their best property.
The Prophet was commanded to fight people until they testify there is no god but Allah, which protects their blood and property; Abu Bakr resolved to fight those withholding Zakat.
Dying, Abu Talib refused the Prophet's plea to profess there is no god but Allah, and verses came on not seeking forgiveness for polytheists and Allah guiding whom He wills.
Whoever dies knowing there is no god but Allah, and meets Him without doubt of this and of the Prophet's mission, enters Paradise and is barred from Hell.
Allah's right is that servants worship without partners, and theirs that He not punish them; the news was withheld lest people rely on it, and the testimony saves from Hell.
One content with Allah as Lord, Islam as religion and Muhammad as Prophet tastes faith, which has over sixty or seventy branches, modesty among them.
Modesty is part of faith and brings nothing but good; Imran grew angry when Bushair set books of wisdom against the Prophet's words on it.
Asked for a word on Islam that would need no other, the Prophet said to affirm faith in Allah and then remain steadfast.
The best in Islam is feeding people and greeting those one knows and does not know, and the best Muslim is he from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe.
Faith's sweetness comes from loving Allah and His Messenger above all, loving for Allah's sake and hating return to unbelief; none believes until the Prophet is dearest to him.
None truly believes until he loves for his brother, or his neighbour, what he loves for himself.
No one whose neighbour is unsafe from him enters Paradise; a believer treats his neighbour well, honours his guest, and speaks good or keeps silent.
Evil should be changed by hand, else tongue, else in the heart, the least of faith, and whoever strives so against those who forsake a prophet's way is a believer.
Faith, understanding and tender hearts are with the people of Yemen, and faith with the Hijaz, while unbelief and harshness lie east, pride among camel owners, calm among shepherds.
None enters Paradise without faith or has faith without loving one another, and spreading the greeting of peace fosters that love.
Religion is sincerity to Allah, His Book, His Messenger and the Muslims' leaders and people; Jarir pledged prayer, Zakat, hearing and obeying, and goodwill to every Muslim.
No one is a believer while he commits fornication, theft, drinking wine or plunder, and repentance may be accepted afterwards.
Lying, breaking promises, betraying trust and abusive disputing are signs of a hypocrite, even one who fasts, prays and claims to be Muslim; having one is a trait of hypocrisy.
Calling a Muslim an unbeliever returns to one of the two; knowingly claiming another man as one's father is unbelief, and claiming what is not one's own earns the Fire.
Detesting one's father is unbelief, and Paradise is forbidden to whoever knowingly claims a man other than his real father as his father.
Abusing a Muslim is an outrage and fighting him is unbelief; at the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet warned not to turn unbelievers after him by striking one another's necks.
Slandering lineage and wailing over the dead are akin to unbelief, and a slave who flees his master commits unbelief, loses protection and has his prayer refused.
After rain, those crediting Allah's mercy believe in Him while those crediting a star disbelieve in Him, and the verse on the setting of the stars came about this.
Loving the Ansar is a sign of faith and hating them a sign of hypocrisy; no believer in Allah and the Last Day bears them a grudge.
Ali swore the Prophet promised him that only a believer would love him and only a hypocrite would bear him a grudge.
The Prophet told women to give charity and seek forgiveness, having seen many women in Hell for cursing and ingratitude to husbands, and named a lack in sense and religion.
When a person prostrates at a verse of prostration, Satan withdraws weeping that man obeyed and earned Paradise while he refused and is doomed to Hell.
Between a man and polytheism and unbelief stands the abandoning of prayer.
The best deeds are faith in Allah, jihad and an accepted Hajj, or prayer on time, kindness to parents and jihad; the costliest slave is best to free.
The gravest sins include associating partners with Allah, killing one's child, adultery with a neighbour's wife, disobeying or abusing parents, false testimony, and the seven destructive sins.
No one with a mustard seed's weight of pride enters Paradise; loving fine dress is not pride, which is rejecting the truth and despising people.
Whoever dies associating anything with Allah enters the Fire, and whoever dies without doing so enters Paradise, even if he committed adultery and theft.
An enemy who says there is no god but Allah must not be killed, as Miqdad and Usama were told; whoever takes up arms against Muslims is not of them.
Finding grain wet inside a heap, the Prophet told its owner to put it on top where people could see, saying whoever deceives is not of him.
Those who strike their cheeks, tear clothes, cry the slogans of ignorance, wail or shave their hair are not of the Prophet's people, as Abu Musa told his wife.
Told of a man who carried tales to the governor, Hudhaifa said he heard the Prophet say that a tale-bearer will not enter Paradise.
Allah will not speak to or purify some on the Day of Resurrection, such as the garment-trailer, giver who reminds, false-oath seller, old adulterer, lying king and proud poor man.
Whoever kills himself is punished by that same means; fighters who did so were of the Fire, and a man bleeding to death from a pierced boil was denied Paradise.
At Khaybar, men hailed as martyrs were in the Fire over a garment stolen from the booty, laces taken were called laces of fire, and only believers enter Paradise.
Tufail's fellow emigrant cut his finger joints in illness and died; in a dream he said Allah forgave him for emigrating, and the Prophet asked pardon for his hands too.
Allah will send a wind from Yemen, softer than silk, that causes the death of everyone with faith the weight of a grain or a speck of dust.
Hasten to good deeds before turmoil like part of a dark night, when a man is a believer by morning and an unbeliever by evening, selling faith for worldly goods.
When the verse against raising voices above the Prophet's came, loud-voiced Thabit b. Qais stayed home thinking himself of the Fire, but the Prophet said he was of Paradise.
One doing good in Islam is not held for deeds of ignorance; Islam, migration and Hajj wipe out past sins, repentant polytheists are forgiven, and Hakim kept his earlier virtues.
When the verse on not mixing faith with wrongdoing troubled the Companions, the Prophet said the wrongdoing meant is associating partners with Allah, as Luqman told his son.
A verse on accounting for hidden thoughts distressed the Companions; told to say 'we hear and obey', they did, and Allah revealed that He burdens no soul beyond capacity.
Allah forgives unspoken, unacted evil thoughts; a good intended is written as one, done as ten to seven hundred, and an evil left undone as nothing or a good.
Thoughts too grave to voice are clear faith; people and Satan will ask who created Allah, and whoever meets this should affirm faith in Allah and seek refuge.
Taking a Muslim's property by false oath, even a twig, earns Hell and Allah's anger; in disputes over land and a well without evidence, the defendant's oath decided.
A man killed defending his property from one who tries to take it is a martyr, and the attacker, if killed, is in the Fire.
A ruler who dies dishonest to his subjects, or does not strive and wish them well, is barred from Paradise, as the dying Ma'qil told Ubaidullah b. Ziyad.
Trustworthiness came down into hearts and will be lifted in sleep, leaving a mark, until a trustworthy man is rare and admired people lack a mustard seed of faith.
The Prophet said trials will be pressed onto hearts, turning them white or black; Hudhaifa told Umar this, adding that a closed door between him and them would be broken.
Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange, so good tidings to the strangers; faith will recede to Medina like a snake into its hole.
The Hour will not come while anyone on earth still says 'Allah, Allah'.
When the Muslims counted were six to seven hundred, the Prophet warned they might be tried, and later some had to pray in secret.
Sa'd urged a share for a man he called a believer; the Prophet said 'or a Muslim', giving some lest Allah throw them into the Fire, though others were dearer.
Abraham asked to see how the dead are revived so his heart might rest; the Prophet said we have more claim to doubt, and spoke of Lot and Joseph's imprisonment.
Every prophet was given a sign people believed in; the Prophet was given the revelation Allah sent him and hoped for the greatest following on the Day of Resurrection.
Any Jew or Christian who hears of the Prophet and dies without believing in what he was sent with will be among the people of the Fire.
Double reward is for one of the People of the Book accepting the Prophet, a slave true to Allah and master, and a man who frees and marries his bondswoman.
Jesus will descend as a just judge, break the cross, kill swine and abolish jizya; wealth will go unaccepted, and he will decline the Muslims' invitation to lead their prayer.
Once the sun rises in the west, or the Dajjal or the beast of the earth appears, late faith avails nothing; till then the sun prostrates nightly under the Throne.
Revelation began with true dreams and the angel in Hira commanding the Prophet to recite; Khadija reassured him, Waraqa recognised it, and after a pause came 'You who are shrouded'.
The Prophet's heart was washed with Zamzam, once as a boy; he rode al-Buraq to Jerusalem, met prophets in the heavens, and fifty daily prayers were reduced to five.
The Prophet described the looks of Moses, Jesus and Abraham from his Night Journey, pictured Moses and Jonah answering Allah in two valleys, and likened Gabriel to Dihya.
In a vision near the Ka'bah the Prophet saw Jesus son of Mary circling it, water dripping from his head, and behind him the Dajjal, blind in the right eye.
When Quraysh denied him, the Prophet was in the Hatim and Allah raised Bait-ul-Maqdis before him, so he described its features while looking at it.
Asleep, the Prophet saw himself circling the Ka'bah and saw the son of Mary, water flowing from his head, and then the Dajjal, bulky, red and blind in one eye.

Questioned by Quraysh about his Night Journey, the Prophet saw Bait-ul-Maqdis raised before him and led the prophets in prayer; at Sidrat-ul-Muntaha he received five prayers and al-Baqara's closing verses.
Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Huraira explain verses of an-Najm about what the Prophet saw as Gabriel, whom he saw in his true form with six hundred wings.
Ibn Abbas says the Prophet saw his Lord with his heart; Aisha calls claiming he saw Him a lie, saying he saw Gabriel; Abu Dharr was told: Light.
Allah does not sleep, nor does it befit Him; He lowers and raises the scale, deeds are raised to Him by night and day, and His veil is light.
In Paradise only the mantle of grandeur over His face screens the Lord; He will lift the veil, and seeing Him will be dearer to its people than any gift.
Believers will see their Lord on Resurrection Day as clearly as sun and moon; each people follows what it worshipped, a bridge spans Hell, and many leave the Fire.
Those burnt in the Fire for their sins who hold a mustard grain of faith are brought out through intercession, cast into the river of life, and sprout like seeds.
The last man out of the Fire and into Paradise keeps asking for more and is granted the world ten times over; Moses asked about Paradise's lowest and highest ranks.
The hypocrites lose their light on the bridge over Hell, and by intercession people leave the Fire for Paradise; Jabir's account turned Yazid al-Faqir from the Khawarij view.
On the Day people seek intercession from Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, who send them to Muhammad; he prostrates, intercedes in stages, and is first at Paradise's gate.
Every prophet has one prayer that is granted; the Prophet reserved his for interceding for his Ummah on the Day of Resurrection, for those who die associating nothing with Allah.
The Prophet recited Abraham's and Jesus's words about their people, raised his hands weeping for his Ummah, and Allah sent Gabriel to say He would please him regarding it.
Asked by a man where his father was, the Prophet said in the Fire, then called him back and said both his own father and the man's are there.
When 'Warn your nearest kindred' was revealed, the Prophet called Quraysh's clans and his family, warning he could not avail them against Allah; Abu Lahab retorted, and his surah followed.
Through the Prophet, Abu Talib, who defended him, will be in the shallowest part of the Fire, in shoes of fire that boil his brain, its lightest punishment.
Ibn Jud'an's keeping ties and feeding the poor will not avail him, the Prophet told Aisha, because he never said: My Lord, pardon my sins on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet declared openly that a certain family among his forefathers' descendants are not his friends; his friends are Allah and the pious believers.
Seventy thousand of the Ummah will enter Paradise without reckoning, faces like the full moon, using no charms, omens or cautery but trusting their Lord; Ukkasha is one of them.
The Prophet hoped his Ummah would be half the people of Paradise, though few as a white hair on a black ox, Gog and Magog being the Fire's thousands.
Cleanliness is half of faith, praising Allah fills the scale, prayer is light, charity proof, endurance brightness, and the Quran a proof for or against you.
No prayer is accepted without ablution, nor charity from pilfered war spoils; one in a state of impurity has no prayer accepted until he performs ablution.
Uthman showed the Prophet's ablution, washing each part three times and wiping the head, and reported that ablution done well, followed by prayer or walking to the mosque, expiates sins.
The five prayers, Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan expiate the sins between them, so long as major sins are avoided.
Ablution done well with two attentive rak'ahs assures Paradise, and testifying after ablution that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His Messenger opens Paradise's eight gates.
Abdullah b. Zaid demonstrated the Prophet's ablution: rinsing mouth and nose, washing face and arms to the elbows, wiping the head front to back, and washing the feet.
In ablution water is snuffed into the nose and the nose cleaned, three times on waking as the devil spends the night there; cleaning with pebbles uses an odd number.
Seeing unwashed heels, the Prophet said woe to the heels from the Fire, ordering complete ablution; a man who missed a nail's breadth was sent back to redo it.
When a believer washes his face, hands and feet in ablution, the sins of each go out with the water, even from under his nails, until he emerges pure.
The Prophet's people will come shining on face, hands and feet from ablution, so he will know them, even those unborn, at his Cistern, where some will be turned away.
The Prophet speaks at the graveyard of people driven from his Cistern; a believer's adornment reaches where ablution reaches, and thorough ablution and waiting for prayer wipe out sins.
The Prophet would have ordered the tooth-stick at every prayer but for burdening people; he used it first on entering his house and on rising for night prayer.
Acts of fitra include circumcision, shaving pubes, cutting nails, plucking armpit hair and clipping the moustache, the last four within forty nights; the beard is grown to differ from polytheists.
The Prophet forbade facing the Qibla when relieving oneself, or wiping with the right hand, bone, dung or under three pebbles; Ibn Umar saw him with his back to it.
The Prophet loved starting from the right in ablution, combing and shoes; relieving oneself on paths or in shade invites cursing, and he cleansed himself with water Anas carried.
Jarir and Hudhaifa saw the Prophet urinate, once standing at a rubbish heap, then perform ablution and wipe over his socks; Hudhaifa disliked Abu Musa's extreme strictness over urine.
Mughira poured water as the Prophet, drawing his arms out under a tight gown, washed and wiped his forelock, turban and socks, which he had put on over clean feet.
Ali gives the limit for wiping over socks: three days and nights for a traveller, one for a resident; at the Conquest the Prophet prayed several prayers with one ablution.
On waking from sleep one must wash the hand three times before putting it in a vessel, for one does not know where it was during the night.
A vessel a dog licks is emptied and washed seven times, with sand or earth; the Prophet ordered dogs killed, then allowed dogs for hunting, herding and guarding crops.
None may urinate in standing water and wash in it, nor bathe in it when junub; the Prophet let a Bedouin finish urinating in the mosque, then had water poured.
When unweaned babies brought to the Prophet urinated on his lap or garment, he sprinkled water over it and did not wash it.
Aisha scraped dried semen off the Prophet's garment or washed it, and he prayed in it; menstrual blood on a garment is scraped, rubbed and rinsed before praying in it.
Passing two graves, the Prophet said their occupants were punished for carrying tales and carelessness about urine, and planted halves of a fresh twig on them hoping for relief.
The Prophet embraced and lay with his menstruating wives over a waist-wrapper or cloth, and called Umm Salama back under his cover when her menses began.
Menstruating Aisha combed and washed the Prophet's head during his I'tikaf and fetched him the mat; he drank and ate where she had, and recited Quran in her lap.
The Jews shunned menstruating women; after the verse on menstruation the Prophet permitted everything except intercourse, and his face changed when two companions proposed no contact like the Jews.
Ali, too shy to ask, sent al-Miqdad: prostatic fluid requires washing the organ and ablution; the Prophet, waking at night, relieved himself, washed face and hands and slept.
After intercourse the Prophet performed ablution before sleeping or eating, sometimes bathing first; one repeating intercourse should perform ablution, and he lay with his wives with a single bath.
Over Aisha's and Umm Salama's surprise, the Prophet told Umm Sulaim a woman seeing fluid after a sexual dream must bathe; it happens, as children resemble whichever parent's fluid prevails.
A Jewish rabbi asked the Prophet where people will be when the earth is changed, about Paradise's first food and drink and a child's sex, then declared him an Apostle.
Aisha and Maimuna describe the Prophet's bath after intercourse: washing hands and private parts, ablution as for prayer, water through hair roots and over the body, feet last, no towel.
The Prophet bathed from one vessel with Aisha, Maimuna or Umm Salama, using about a Sa' for bathing and a Mudd for ablution; Aisha showed the bath behind a curtain.
The Prophet poured three handfuls over his head and told Umm Salama she need not undo her plaits; Aisha faulted Ibn Amr for ordering women to undo theirs.
Asked how to bathe after menstruation, the Prophet taught the bath and a musk-scented piece of cotton for purifying; Aisha quietly explained it is applied to the traces of blood.
Fatimah b. Abu Hubaish and Umm Habiba, whose bleeding continued, were told it is a vein, not menstruation: leave prayer for the usual days, then bathe and pray.
Asking whether the questioner is a Haruriya, Aisha says menstruating women were told to make up missed fasts but not missed prayers.
Fatimah and Maimuna screened the Prophet while he bathed; a man must not look at another man's private parts nor a woman at a woman's, nor share one cover.
The Children of Israel bathed naked and taunted Moses, who bathed alone, until a stone ran off with his clothes and they saw he had no defect.
Carrying stones for the Ka'ba, the Prophet fainted on baring himself and was never seen naked again; he told Miswar not to walk naked, and sought cover when relieving himself.
Some reports require bathing only on emission, ablution sufficing otherwise; others, like Aisha's answer to Abu Musa, require it on intercourse itself; the Prophet abrogated some commands by others.
The Prophet ordered ablution after eating what fire has touched, yet he ate goat's shoulder, meat and roasted liver and then prayed without ablution.
The Prophet prayed after eating meat without ablution; ablution is due after camel meat, optional after mutton, and one in doubt leaves prayer only on a sound or smell.
Seeing a dead goat given in charity to Maimuna's freed slave-girl, the Prophet said only eating it is forbidden; tanning makes its skin pure, even skins brought by Magians.
Tayammum was revealed when Aisha's lost necklace stranded people waterless; Ammar learned wiping face and palms suffices; the Prophet wiped face and hands at a wall before returning a greeting.
Abu Huraira and Hudhaifa slipped away to bathe after meeting the Prophet while sexually defiled; he told them a believer is never defiled.
Aisha says the Prophet remembered Allah at all moments.
Coming out of the privy and offered food, the Prophet ate without ablution, saying he was not about to pray.
On entering the privy the Prophet sought refuge in Allah from wicked and noxious things.
The Prophet's whispered talk with a man delayed the prayer until the people dozed off; the Companions dozed and then prayed without performing ablution.
Seeking a way to announce prayer in Medina, Muslims proposed a bell, horn or fire; Bilal was told to call, doubling the Adhan's phrases and saying the Iqama's once.
Bilal and the blind Ibn Umm Maktum called the Adhan; the Prophet attacked at dawn only where he heard none, and said a goatherd calling it had left the Fire.
Those hearing the mu'adhdhin should repeat his words, then bless the Prophet and ask al-Wasila, a rank in Paradise, for him; such responses bring his intercession, forgiveness and Paradise.
At the call to prayer and the Iqama Satan flees, breaking wind, then returns to distract the worshipper until he does not know how much he has prayed.
The Prophet raised his hands to his shoulders or ears when beginning the prayer, before bowing and on rising from it, but not between the prostrations.
Abu Huraira said takbir at every bending and rising, calling his prayer the closest to the Prophet's, and Ali's prayer with takbir reminded Imran of the Prophet's.
Prayer without the Fatiha is not credited; Allah divides it between Himself and His servant verse by verse, and Abu Huraira says it suffices, though reciting more is better.
A man sent back three times to pray again was taught to perform ablution, face the Qibla, say takbir, recite, and bow, prostrate and sit calmly.
The Prophet felt a man reciting behind him was disputing his recitation; Anas never heard the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar or Uthman recite Bismillah aloud.
Waking from a doze, the Prophet recited a newly revealed surah: al-Kauthar is a canal his Lord promised him, a cistern his people will reach, some turned away for innovating.
Wa'il saw the Prophet raise his hands, place right over left and prostrate between his palms; he taught the tashahhud like a surah, and Abu Musa relayed following the imam.
Asked how to bless him, the Prophet taught asking Allah to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham's family; whoever blesses him once, Allah blesses ten times.
When the imam says Allah listens to him who praises Him, or ends the Fatiha, those behind respond with praise and Amin; whoever matches the angels is forgiven past sins.
Hurt by a fall from his horse or ill, the Prophet led prayer sitting and seated those behind: the imam is to be followed, never preceded, sitting when he sits.
In his last illness the Prophet had Abu Bakr lead the prayer despite Aisha's objections, once prayed seated beside him, and on Monday looked at the rows and died.
In the Prophet's absence Abu Bakr and Abd al-Rahman b. Auf began leading the prayer before he arrived; to alert the imam men glorify Allah, while clapping is for women.
The Prophet told people to perform their bowing and prostration well, saying he saw them behind his back as he saw in front.
The Prophet forbade preceding the imam in bowing, prostration or standing, said he had seen Paradise and Hell, and warned Allah may turn a head raised first into an ass's.
Worshippers must not lift their eyes to the sky in prayer or wave their hands at the salutation like headstrong horses' tails, but be calm and form rows like angels.
The Prophet straightened the rows like an arrow, warning that crooked rows bring dissension among hearts, and wanted the sedate and prudent nearest him.
If people knew the first row's merit they would draw lots for it; men's best rows are first, women's last, and women were once told to lift heads after men.
The Prophet said not to prevent women from going to the mosque, even at night, when they ask; Ibn Umar harshly rebuked his son for saying he would prevent them.
A woman coming to the mosque or the Isha prayer must not wear perfume; Aisha said that had the Prophet seen what women introduced, he would have prevented them.
Ibn Abbas says the verse on praying neither too loudly nor too low came while the Prophet hid in Mecca and polytheists reviled the Quran; Aisha says it concerns supplication.
The Prophet moved his tongue to memorise revelation as Gabriel brought it, until Allah told him not to hasten, for He would collect it; then he listened and afterwards recited.
Told by a verse not to move his tongue in haste, the Prophet listened attentively while Gabriel recited and, when Gabriel left, recited as he had.
Jinn heard the Prophet reciting at the morning prayer and believed; one night he went with their inviter, recited the Quran to them, and named bones as their food.
In noon and afternoon prayers the Prophet recited al-Fatiha and a surah in the first two rak'ahs, longer than the last two, as Sa'd told Umar he too did.
In the morning prayer the Prophet recited Surah Qaf, al-Mu'minun and the like, sixty to a hundred verses, prolonging it more than the noon and afternoon prayers.
The Prophet recited Surat al-Tur and the surah Umm al-Fadl last heard from him in the evening prayer, and 'By the Fig' in the night prayer on a journey.
When Mu'adh, after praying with the Prophet, led his people in a long night prayer with al-Baqara, the Prophet rebuked him for trying them and named shorter surahs to recite.
An imam must be brief for the weak, sick, aged and busy, but alone one may lengthen; the Prophet's prayer was brief yet perfect, shortened when a child cried.
The Prophet's standing, bowing, rising, prostrating and sitting were nearly balanced, and he and Anas paused after bowing and between prostrations so long that people thought they had forgotten.
Behind the Prophet no one bent down for prostration until he had placed his forehead on the ground; only then did they follow him.
On rising from bowing the Prophet praised his Lord with praise filling the heavens and earth, saying none can withhold what He gives, and asked to be purified with snow.
The Prophet said only good visions remain of prophethood's glad tidings and forbade reciting the Quran in bowing and prostration, which are for glorifying the Lord and supplication.
A servant is nearest his Lord in prostration, so supplicate there; bowing and prostrating, the Prophet glorified Allah, asked forgiveness and sought refuge in His pleasure from His anger.
Frequent prostration raises a degree and removes a sin with each one, and the Prophet told Rabi'a, who asked for his company in Paradise, to help him by prostrating often.
The Prophet was commanded to prostrate on seven bones, forehead, hands, knees and feet, and not to fold back hair or clothing; Ibn Abbas undid a man's plaited hair.
In prostration the forearms are not spread like a dog's: palms down, elbows raised, the Prophet's arms so wide his armpits showed; Aisha described his prayer from takbir to taslim.
A sutra the height of a saddle's back suffices; the Prophet prayed facing a planted spear, staff or his camel, while people and animals passed beyond it.
Nearly of age, Ibn Abbas rode a donkey in front of the row as the Prophet led prayer at Mina, then joined it, and no one objected.
A worshipper must turn back, forcibly if needed, anyone passing before him; a passer knowing his burden would rather stand forty; the Prophet prayed near a wall or pillar.
Without a saddle-high sutra a passing woman, ass or black dog cuts the prayer; Aisha objected that the Prophet prayed at night while she lay between him and the qibla.
Asked about praying in one garment, the Prophet asked if everyone had two, and he himself prayed in a single garment, its ends crossed over his shoulders.
The first mosque on earth was al-Masjid al-Haram, then al-Aqsa forty years later, and wherever the time of prayer comes, the earth is a mosque.
The Prophet and his community were given what others were not: mission to all mankind, lawful spoils, the earth as mosque and purifier, terror in enemies' hearts, intercession, concise speech.
Arriving in Medina, the Prophet prayed in sheepfolds until the Banu al-Najjar gave their land for Allah's reward and he had it cleared to build the mosque.
After sixteen or seventeen months of praying towards Bait-ul-Maqdis, the qibla was changed to the Ka'ba, and people at prayer, told of it, turned round in mid-prayer.
The Prophet called builders of places of worship on pious men's graves the worst of creatures, cursed Jews and Christians who took their prophets' graves as mosques, and forbade it.
When people objected to Uthman rebuilding the Prophet's mosque, he cited the Prophet: whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds for him a house like it in Paradise.
Ibn Mas'ud bowed with palms between his thighs, but Sa'd said this was later replaced by palms on the knees; Ibn Abbas called a sitting hard on the foot sunnah.
Talking, even returning a greeting, is not fitting in prayer, which is glorification, takbir and recitation; a verse commanded silence, and the Prophet only gestured when greeted while praying.
A wicked jinn, in another report Iblis with a flame of fire, tried to disrupt the Prophet's prayer; he would have bound him but for his brother Solomon's supplication.
The Prophet led prayer carrying his granddaughter Umama, prayed on his new pulpit to teach the prayer, forbade hands on the waist, and allowed removing pebbles only once.
The Prophet scraped spittle off the qibla wall and told worshippers to spit only left, under the foot; spitting in the mosque is a sin, expiated by burying it.
Anas said the Prophet prayed in his shoes, and a garment with designs that distracted the Prophet in prayer he sent to Abu Jahm for a plain one.
When supper is served as the prayer begins, eat first rather than hurry to pray; Aisha cited the Prophet: no prayer is right with food present or when nature calls.
Whoever eats garlic, onion or leek should keep away from the mosque, for the smell harms angels and people, though the Prophet would not forbid what Allah made lawful.
One who hears a man calling out in the mosque for something lost should say, May Allah not restore it to you, for mosques were not built for this.
If the devil confuses a worshipper's count, or he misses the sitting after two rak'ahs as the Prophet did, he prostrates twice sitting, building on what he is sure of.
The Prophet, after praying five rak'ahs or adding or omitting something, made two prostrations, saying he forgot as others forget, and told the doubtful to aim at what is correct.
When the Prophet ended prayer after two or three rak'ahs, a long-armed man asked whether it was shortened or he had forgotten; he completed it and made two prostrations.
The Prophet and those with him prostrated on reciting verses of prostration, including al-Najm and 'When the heaven burst asunder', though once, when Zaid recited al-Najm, he did not.
Sitting for the tashahhud, the Prophet placed his hands on his thighs or knees and pointed with his forefinger, and ended the prayer with salutations to the right and left.
In the Prophet's time the end of the obligatory prayer was known by the takbir and the remembrance of Allah said aloud.
Jewish women told Aisha of torment in the grave; after a revelation the Prophet confirmed that the dead are tried in their graves and sought refuge from it in prayer.
In prayer, after the tashahhud, the Prophet sought and taught refuge from the torment of Hell and the grave, the trial of life and death, the Dajjal, sin and debt.
After the salutation the Prophet asked forgiveness thrice, said 'Thou art Peace', and affirmed there is no god but Allah alone, none withholding what He gives; Ibn Zubair said likewise.
The Prophet taught the poor emigrants to glorify, praise and magnify Allah thirty-three times each after every prayer; the wealthy copied it, and sins abundant as sea foam are forgiven.
Between the opening takbir and the recitation the Prophet silently asked Allah to remove and wash away his sins, but in the second rak'ah he began al-Fatiha without pause.
Two men said words of praise in prayer; the Prophet said twelve angels vied to take one man's words up and heaven's doors opened for the other's.
When the iqama is said, come to prayer walking calmly, not running, pray what you catch with the imam and complete what you missed.
At the iqama people were not to stand till they saw the Prophet; once he left the formed rows to bathe, and Bilal said the iqama only on seeing him.
Whoever catches one rak'ah of the prayer, with the imam in one wording, has caught the prayer.
Whoever catches one rak'ah of the dawn prayer before sunrise, or of the afternoon prayer before sunset, has caught that prayer.
When Umar b. Abd al-Aziz delayed prayer, Urwa reported Gabriel leading the Prophet in the five prayers, and Aisha his afternoon prayer while sunlight was in her room.
The Prophet set the limits of each prayer's time, and showed an inquirer by praying early one day and late the next, saying the time lies between.
The noon prayer is delayed in intense heat till it cools, for such heat is Hell's exhalation; the Fire, complaining, was allowed two breaths, in winter and summer.
The Prophet prayed noon once the sun declined and did not respond to complaints about praying on scorching ground; in the heat some prostrated on their spread cloth.
The afternoon prayer was prayed early enough to reach Quba or cook and eat a camel before sunset; the hypocrite waits till the sun is between the devil's horns.
Whoever misses the afternoon prayer is as though he has been deprived of his family and his property.
At Ahzab the enemy kept the Prophet from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, till sunset, and he asked Allah to fill their houses and graves with fire.
Aisha had her copy of the Quran written 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer', saying she heard it so from the Prophet.
At the Ditch Umar and the Prophet had both missed the afternoon prayer; the Prophet made ablution, prayed it after sunset, then prayed the evening prayer.
Angels gather at the dawn and afternoon prayers; believers will see their Lord as they see the moon, and whoever keeps these two prayers will enter Paradise, not the Fire.
The Prophet prayed the evening prayer as soon as the sun had set, and afterwards one could still see where his arrow fell.
The Prophet once delayed the night prayer till many slept, saying no others waited for it and he would pray then were it not a burden on his community.
The Prophet sometimes delayed Isha until people slept or near midnight, said those waiting were in prayer, and would have ordered that hour were it not hard on his Ummah.
The Prophet told people not to let the bedouins prevail over the name of their night prayer, which is Isha in the Book of Allah, though bedouins call it Atama.
Believing women prayed the morning prayer with the Prophet and went home wrapped in their mantles, unrecognisable in the darkness before dawn.
Jabir and Abu Barza described the Prophet's prayer times, from noon in the midday heat to dawn in early darkness; he disliked sleeping before Isha and talking after it.
The Prophet told Abu Dharr that under rulers who delay prayer beyond its time he should pray at its proper time and count praying with them as voluntary.
Prayer in congregation is twenty-five or twenty-seven degrees more excellent than prayer said alone.
The Prophet said he had thought of burning the houses of men absent from congregational and Friday prayers, and that the night and morning prayers weigh most on hypocrites.
A blind man hearing the call was told to answer it; Ibn Mas'ud said only known hypocrites or the sick stayed away; one leaving after the call disobeyed the Prophet.
Praying Isha in congregation is like praying half the night and the morning prayer like praying all night; whoever prays the morning prayer is under Allah's protection.
The Prophet prayed in blind Itban's house to mark a prayer place for him, and there said Allah forbids the Fire to whoever declares His oneness seeking His pleasure.
The Prophet led Anas and his household in prayer at home, Anas standing behind him with an orphan or alone at his right, and the women behind them.
The Prophet prayed and prostrated on a small mat, his garment touching Maimuna beside him when he prostrated.
Congregational prayer exceeds praying at home or market by over twenty degrees; each step to the mosque raises a degree, and angels pray for those waiting there in ablution.
Walking far to prayer brings greater reward; the Prophet told a distant Ansari and Banu Salama their steps were recorded, each erasing a sin or raising a degree.
The five daily prayers wipe away sins just as bathing five times a day in a river at one's door would leave no dirt.
Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or evening, Allah prepares a feast for him in Paradise each morning or evening.
After the dawn prayer the Prophet sat in his place until the sun had risen, while his companions talked of the days of ignorance and laughed and he only smiled.
The places dearest to Allah are the mosques and the most hateful to Him are the markets.
The one best versed in the Quran leads the prayer, then the most knowing of the Sunnah, earliest emigrant or eldest; the Prophet told young visitors their oldest should lead.
After bowing in prayer the Prophet asked Allah to rescue helpless Muslims, send famine on Mudar and curse other tribes, stopping once they were rescued or a verse came.
For a month in the dawn prayer, after bowing, the Prophet cursed Ri'l, Dhakwan, Lihyan and Usayya, who killed the seventy reciters at Bi'r Ma'una, and then abandoned it.
The Prophet recited Qunut in the dawn and evening prayers, and in prayer cursed Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and Usayya, saying Allah pardoned Ghifar and protected Aslam.
On journeys the Prophet and his companions slept past sunrise, moved on, then prayed the dawn prayer; he said sleep is no fault, and a little water sufficed everyone.
Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it should pray it when he remembers, its only expiation, for Allah said to observe prayer for His remembrance.
Prayer was prescribed as two rak'ahs and kept so on journeys; shortening is Allah's charity, and the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman prayed only two rak'ahs travelling.
The Prophet shortened to two rak'ahs at Dhu'l-Hulaifa and after three miles or farsakhs, and kept praying two rak'ahs during a ten-day stay in Mecca until returning to Medina.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar prayed two rak'ahs at Mina, as did Uthman at first before praying four, which Ibn Mas'ud regretted; Ibn Umar prayed four behind the imam.
On cold, windy or rainy nights the Prophet had the caller tell people to pray in their dwellings, as Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas did, even on a rainy Friday.
On journeys the Prophet prayed voluntary prayers and witr on his mount facing wherever it went, but not obligatory ones; the verse on Allah's face wherever you turn concerns this.
When hurrying on a journey the Prophet combined sunset with Isha and noon with afternoon, delaying the first prayer to the time of the second.
The Prophet combined noon with afternoon and sunset with Isha in Medina without fear, rain or journey, and on the Tabuk expedition, so his Ummah would not face hardship.
After prayer the Prophet turned to the left as well as to the right, and companions liked to stand at his right so his face would turn to them.
Once the iqama is given only the obligatory prayer is prayed; the Prophet questioned men who prayed alone after the dawn prayer had begun.
Entering the mosque one asks Allah to open the doors of His mercy and prays two rak'ahs before sitting, as the Prophet told Jabir and did after journeys.
Aisha said the Prophet prayed the forenoon prayer only after journeys, or prayed four rak'ahs or more; Umm Hani saw him pray eight rak'ahs when Mecca was conquered.
Charity is due on every bone each morning and two forenoon rak'ahs suffice; Abu Huraira and Abu Darda were told to fast three days monthly, pray forenoon and witr.
The Prophet prayed two short rak'ahs between the call and iqama of the dawn prayer, kept them more than any voluntary prayer, and said they are better than the world.
In the two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer the Prophet recited 'Say: O unbelievers' and 'Say: Allah is One', or verses from al-Baqara and Al Imran.
Allah builds a house in Paradise for whoever prays twelve voluntary rak'ahs a day, and Ibn Umar listed those he prayed with the Prophet before and after the obligatory prayers.
Aisha described the Prophet's long night prayer standing or sitting, bowing from the position he recited in, and in old age reciting seated but standing to recite before bowing.
In his last year or two the Prophet prayed most voluntary prayers sitting; he said a seated prayer is worth half, but he is not like others.
Aisha said the Prophet prayed eleven or thirteen rak'ahs at night with witr, in Ramadan or not, then two short rak'ahs before dawn, and that his heart did not sleep.
The Prophet slept early and rose late in the night or at cockcrow to pray, loved regular deeds, and after the two dawn rak'ahs talked with Aisha or lay down.
The Prophet prayed witr every night, early, at midnight or late, finishing it by dawn, and woke Aisha to pray her witr.
Aisha told Sa'd b. Hisham the Prophet's character was the Quran, night prayer became voluntary after a year, and described his witr of nine, later seven, rak'ahs.
When illness or sleep kept the Prophet from night prayer he prayed twelve rak'ahs by day, and a night portion of Quran missed is recorded if recited before noon.
The Prophet said the prayer of the penitent is observed when young weaned camels feel the heat of the sun.
Night prayer is offered in pairs of rak'ahs, and one fearing dawn adds a single rak'ah; witr is one rak'ah at the end of the night prayer, prayed before morning.
Night prayer is in pairs closed by one rak'ah; observe witr before morning, early if one may not wake, otherwise at the end of the night, which is witnessed.
The most excellent prayer is the one in which the standing is longest.
Every night there is an hour in which any Muslim who asks Allah for good in this world and the next is given it.
Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven, asking who will call on Him, ask of Him or seek His forgiveness, until daybreak.
Praying at night in Ramadan or on Lailat-ul-Qadr with faith and hope of reward brings forgiveness of past sins; the Prophet stopped leading Ramadan night prayer lest it become obligatory.
Ubayy b. Ka'b swore that Lailat-ul-Qadr is in Ramadan, on the twenty-seventh night, and that the sun rises next morning bright without rays.
Spending a night at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas joined the Prophet's night prayer, was moved from his left to his right, and heard him pray for light within and around him.
At night the Prophet recited the last verses of Al Imran, prayed thirteen rak'ahs with witr, and moved Ibn Abbas from his left to his right.
On a journey the Prophet prayed in one garment tied at opposite ends and moved Jabir, standing behind him, to his right.
The Prophet began his night prayer with two short rak'ahs and told others to do the same.
Rising to pray at night the Prophet praised Allah as Light and Lord of the heavens and earth and asked guidance and forgiveness, with set words for bowing and prostrating.
At night the Prophet recited al-Baqara, al-Nisa and Al Imran before bowing, pausing to glorify, ask and seek refuge, and prayed so long Abdullah thought of sitting.
The devil urinates in the ear of an all-night sleeper and ties three knots on sleepers, undone by remembrance, ablution and prayer; the Prophet urged Ali and Fatimah to pray.
Pray some prayers at home and do not make houses graves; a man's prayer at home is best except the obligatory, and Satan flees a house where al-Baqara is recited.
Allah loves best deeds done constantly, even if small; the Prophet had Zainab's prayer rope untied and, about a woman praying all night, said to do what one can sustain.
Whoever dozes in prayer, or whose tongue falters reciting the Quran at night, should sleep first, for he may not know whether he is asking pardon or reviling himself.
A man's recitation reminded the Prophet of verses he had been made to forget; keep refreshing the Quran, which escapes faster than hobbled camels, and never say 'I forgot it'.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to a prophet reciting the Quran in a sweet voice, and Abu Musa was given a voice like those of David's family.
In the year of the Conquest of Mecca the Prophet recited Surat al-Fath on his mount while travelling, repeating the words, as Ibn Mughaffal later demonstrated.
A cloud that frightened a horse while its owner recited al-Kahf was tranquillity descending, and the canopy of lamps over Usaid b. Hudair as he recited was angels listening.
A believer who recites the Quran is like a sweet, fragrant orange; the proficient reciter is with the noble recording angels, and one who falters in it has two rewards.
Allah commanded the Prophet to recite to Ubayy, who wept at being named; the Prophet asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite to him and wept at a verse of Surat al-Nisa'.
In Hims Ibn Mas'ud recited Surah Yusuf, which the Prophet had approved; the man who denied it smelled of wine, so Ibn Mas'ud lashed him with the prescribed punishment.
Three verses recited in prayer, or verses taught or recited in the mosque each morning, are better than as many large she-camels.
The Quran will intercede for its reciters on Resurrection Day, and al-Baqara and Al Imran will come like two clouds or flocks of birds pleading for those who recited them.
An angel announced to the Prophet two lights given to no prophet before, the Fatiha and the end of al-Baqara, whose last two verses suffice whoever recites them at night.
Whoever learns by heart ten verses of Surah al-Kahf, from its beginning or, in one narration, its end, will be protected from the Dajjal.
Ubayy b. Ka'b named 'Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Eternal' as the greatest verse in the Book of Allah, and the Prophet praised his knowledge.
'Say: He is Allah, One' equals a third of the Quran, and Allah loves the expedition leader who ended his recitation in prayer with it because it describes the Compassionate.
The Prophet said verses unlike any seen before had come down: the Mu'awwadhatain, 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the dawn' and 'with the Lord of men'.
Envy is justified only of two: one given the Quran who recites it night and day, or wisdom he judges and teaches by, and one given wealth who spends it.
Umar, told that his collector had appointed a freed slave versed in the Book of Allah, quoted the Prophet: by this Book Allah exalts some peoples and degrades others.
Umar and Ubayy objected to others' different recitations, but the Prophet approved each, saying the Quran was sent down in seven modes, granted at his request to ease his people.
Ibn Mas'ud told a man who recited all the mufassal surahs in one rak'ah that he rushed like poetry, recalling how the Prophet paired surahs, two in each rak'ah.
The Prophet read 'muddakir' with a d, and Abu Darda' heard him recite 'By the night when it covers' with 'the male and the female', as Ibn Mas'ud did.
The Prophet forbade praying after the dawn prayer till sunrise, after Asr till sunset, and as the sun rises, stands at midday or sets, for it rises between Satan's horns.
Amr b. Abasa met the Prophet hiding in Mecca, later joined him in Medina and learned when to pray or refrain, and how ablution and prayer wash away sins.
Aisha said the Prophet never left two rak'ahs after Asr in her house; he told Umm Salama they made up the two after noon, missed while receiving a delegation.
People prayed two rak'ahs between the sunset call and Maghrib prayer, which the Prophet saw but neither ordered nor forbade; between adhan and iqamah is a prayer for whoever wishes.
In danger the Prophet led two groups or rows that took turns praying and facing the enemy; at Dhat ar-Riqa' he prayed four rak'ahs and each group two.
Whoever comes to the Friday prayer should bathe, use siwak and perfume; Umar rebuked a latecomer who only made ablution, and the earliest comer is like one sacrificing a camel.
Telling a companion to be quiet while the Imam delivers the Friday sermon is itself idle talk.
On Friday there is a short time when Allah grants any good a Muslim asks in prayer, placed by one report between the Imam sitting down and the prayer's end.
Friday, the best day, is when Adam was created and the Hour will come; Allah guided this last community to it, while the Jews took Saturday and the Christians Sunday.
Angels at the mosque doors record Friday arrivals in order, as if sacrificing a camel down to an egg; whoever listens silently is forgiven till next Friday, plus three days.
The Prophet led the Friday prayer when the sun had passed the meridian; afterwards people rested their camels and took their siesta and lunch, finding little shade from the walls.
The Prophet delivered two Friday sermons standing, sitting between them, reciting the Quran and exhorting people; Jabir b. Samura called anyone claiming he preached sitting a liar.
When a caravan came during the Friday sermon, all but twelve left the Prophet standing and a verse came down about it, which Ka'b cited against a seated preacher.
From his pulpit the Prophet warned that people must stop neglecting the Friday prayer, or Allah will seal their hearts and they will be among the negligent.
The Prophet's prayer and sermon were moderate; preaching, his eyes reddened and voice rose like one warning of an enemy, calling Allah's Book the best speech and every innovation error.
Dimad came to Mecca to cure the Prophet of a supposed spell, heard his words of praise and testimony, and pledged allegiance on Islam for himself and his people.
Ammar said a long prayer and short sermon show understanding, as the Prophet taught; the Prophet called a preacher who said 'whoever disobeys both of them' a bad speaker.
On the pulpit the Prophet recited the Quran, including Surah Qaf every Friday, and gestured only with his forefinger, as Umara reminded Bishr b. Marwan, who raised his hands.
Whoever arrives while the Imam is preaching should pray two short rak'ahs, as the Prophet told Sulaik Ghatafani; once he left his sermon to teach a stranger the religion.
In the Friday prayer the Prophet recited al-Jumu'a and al-Munafiqun, or al-A'la and al-Ghashiya as on the Eids, and in Friday's dawn prayer al-Sajda and al-Insan.
After the Friday prayer the Prophet prayed two rak'ahs at home and told people to pray four, without joining it to another prayer before talking or going out.
The Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman prayed Eid before the sermon, without adhan or iqamah; the Prophet then urged the women to give alms, and they gave rings.
The Prophet commanded that young, secluded and menstruating women be brought out for the two Eids, the menstruating staying away from the prayer place but joining the supplication.
On Eid the Prophet prayed two rak'ahs, nothing before or after, and told the women to give alms; in Eid prayers he recited Qaf and 'The Hour drew near'.
On Eid the Prophet stopped Abu Bakr scolding two girls singing and drumming, saying every people has a festival, and let Aisha watch Abyssinians play with spears in the mosque.
Praying for rain at the prayer place, the Prophet faced the Qibla, turned his mantle round and prayed two rak'ahs, raising his hands so high his armpits showed.
Asked during the Friday sermon, the Prophet prayed for rain and it rained a week; asked again, he prayed it fall around Medina, not on it, and it cleared.
The Prophet let rain fresh from his Lord touch his body, but feared storm wind and dark clouds might be a calamity, like the wind that destroyed 'Ad.
In the eclipse prayer the Prophet bowed twice each rak'ah, then said sun and moon are signs not eclipsed for anyone's death or birth; he had seen Paradise and Hell.
The eclipse prayer, called in congregation and recited aloud, had two rak'ahs of two or three bowings each and four prostrations, with remembrance of Allah till the sun cleared.
After a Jewess spoke of the grave's torment, the Prophet led an eclipse prayer, then said people are tried in graves like the Dajjal's turmoil, and sought refuge from it.
Praying during eclipses, one on the day Ibrahim died, the Prophet was shown Paradise and Hell, where a woman suffered for starving a cat and a man dragged his intestines.
After the eclipse prayer, Asma' heard the Prophet say people will be tried in their graves and asked about him, the believer affirming him, the hypocrite not knowing.
Perturbed by an eclipse, the Prophet took a woman's garment by mistake, then stood so long that Asma' wished to sit and a newcomer would think he had not bowed.
After a long eclipse prayer the Prophet said he reached for grapes in Paradise and saw Hell, most of its people women, for their ingratitude to husbands and to kindness.
Ibn Abbas reported four bowings in each of the two eclipse rak'ahs and Amr b. al-As two, Aisha saying she never saw longer bowing and prostration.
Eclipses are signs by which Allah frightens His servants, not for anyone's death, as people said when Ibrahim died; on seeing one, pray, supplicate and remember Allah till it clears.
The Prophet said to prompt those who are dying to say 'There is no god but Allah'.
Whoever, hit by calamity, says 'We belong to Allah and to Him we return' is given better; Umm Salama said it when Abu Salama died and married the Prophet.
Closing the dead Abu Salama's eyes, the Prophet said sight follows the departing soul, told the family to pray only for good as angels say amen, and prayed for him.
The Prophet stopped Umm Salama's planned mourning, yet wept at his daughter's dying child and at the sick Sa'd b. Ubada, saying Allah punishes for the tongue, not tears.
Told to fear Allah and endure, a woman weeping over her child rebuffed the unrecognised Prophet; when she apologised he said endurance is shown at the first blow.
When Umar was wounded and Hafsa and Suhaib lamented him, he reminded them that the Prophet said the dead is punished because of the living's weeping over him.
Ibn Umar taught the dead is punished for his family's lamenting; Aisha replied the Prophet said it of an unbeliever or a dead Jew, citing that none bears another's burden.
One lamented is punished for it; wailing is a pre-Islamic habit, an unrepentant wailing woman will stand at Resurrection in pitch garments; the Prophet forbade Ja'far's women to lament.
Women pledged to the Prophet not to wail, though only five kept it, with one exception for Umm Atiyya; women were forbidden, though not absolutely, to follow the bier.
The Prophet had his daughter Zainab washed an odd number of times, right side first, camphor in the last wash, hair in three plaits, and gave his undergarment for her.
The Prophet told the women washing his daughter's body to begin on the right side and with the parts washed in ablution.
Mus'ab, killed at Uhud, had too short a cloak, grass covering his feet; the Prophet was shrouded in three white cotton sheets, no shirt or turban; shroud the dead well.
The Prophet told people to hasten with a funeral: a good person is brought sooner to good, and from an evil one they rid themselves.
Attending a funeral until the prayer earns one qirat and until burial two, each like Uhud; Ibn Umar, after Aisha confirmed Abu Huraira's report, said they had missed many qirats.
If a hundred Muslims, or forty who associate nothing with Allah, pray over a dead Muslim, their intercession is accepted; Ibn Abbas brought out his son once forty gathered.
Paradise is certain for a dead person people praise, Hell for one they condemn, as they are Allah's witnesses; a believer's death relieves him, a wicked one's relieves others.
The Prophet announced the Negus's death on the day he died, told them to ask pardon for their brother, and led the prayer over him in rows with four takbirs.
The Prophet prayed with four takbirs over graves after burial, including the mosque sweeper's, whose death he was not told of; Zaid once said five takbirs, as the Prophet had.
Stand when a bier passes, even a Jew's, until it passes or is set down, nor sit while following it; Ali said the Prophet stood at first, then later sat.
Over the dead, the Prophet asked Allah to forgive him, cleanse him of faults, admit him to the Garden and shield him from the torment of the grave and Fire.
Leading the funeral prayer for a woman who died in childbirth, the Prophet stood level with the middle of her body.
After Ibn Dahdah's funeral prayer the Prophet rode back on an unsaddled horse as people walked and ran around him, and spoke of fruit bunches in Paradise for Ibn Dahdah.
Sa'd asked for a niche grave with bricks like the Prophet's, where a red cloth was placed; the Prophet ordered graves levelled and images obliterated.
The Prophet forbade plastering graves, building over them, sitting on them or praying towards them, saying that sitting on live coals is better than sitting on a grave.
Criticised for having Sa'd b. Abu Waqqas's bier brought into the mosque for prayer, Aisha said the Prophet had offered the funeral prayer of Suhail b. Baida' in the mosque.
The Prophet went by night to al-Baqi' to greet its dead and ask forgiveness for them, as Gabriel commanded, Aisha secretly following, and taught a greeting for graveyards.
Allowed to visit his mother's grave but not to seek forgiveness for her, the Prophet wept, and permitted visiting graves, which recall death, and keeping sacrificial meat.
The Prophet did not offer the funeral prayer over a man who had killed himself with a broad-headed arrow.
No Zakat is due below five wasqs of dates or grain, five camels or five uqiyas of silver; river- or rain-watered crops owe a tenth, camel-watered a twentieth.
No Zakat is due from a Muslim on his slave or horse, except the charity of Fitr for a slave.
When Ibn Jamil, Khalid b. Walid and Abbas refused Zakat to Umar, the Prophet faulted Ibn Jamil, defended Khalid's armour kept for Allah, and took Abbas's due upon himself.
Zakat-ul-Fitr is one sa' of dates, barley, cheese or raisins for every Muslim, free or slave, paid before the prayer; Abu Sa'id rejected Mu'awiya's smaller measure of wheat.
Withholders of dues on gold, silver, camels, cattle or sheep are branded or trampled on Resurrection Day, treasure chasing them as a bald snake; horses bring reward, cover or burden.
Bedouins complaining that Zakat collectors wronged them were told to please the collectors, and Jarir said every collector left him pleased after that.
The very rich are losers unless generous; the Prophet would keep nothing of an Uhud of gold but for debt; Gabriel said whoever dies associating nothing with Allah enters Paradise.
Abu Dharr warned Quraysh hoarders of branding with heated stones, recalled the Prophet's wish to spend an Uhud of gold, and said to take gifts unless they cost one's religion.
Allah tells the son of Adam to spend and He will spend on him, for His right hand is full and spending day and night does not diminish it.
The best dinar is spent on one's family, withholding food from one's slaves is sin enough, and a man was told to spend on himself first, then family, then relatives.
After the verse on giving what you love, Abu Talha gave his garden Bairaha, passed to relatives on the Prophet's advice; charity to kin, even a husband, earns double reward.
Umm Salama was told she is rewarded for spending on Abu Salama's sons, and a Muslim's spending on his family, seeking Allah's reward, counts as charity.
Asma' asked whether to treat kindly her polytheist mother, who came to her during the treaty with Quraysh, and the Prophet told her to do so.
A man whose mother died suddenly without a will was told she would be rewarded if he gave charity on her behalf.
Every good act is charity: glorifying Allah, enjoining good, lawful intimacy with a wife, a good word, removing harm from the path, helping the needy, or refraining from evil.
Every morning two angels pray, one asking Allah to give more to the one who spends and the other to destroy the one who withholds.
A time will come when wealth overflows and none accepts charity, a man is followed by forty women, and the earth casts out gold and silver that is left untouched.
Allah accepts charity only from honest earnings, and takes even a date with His right hand, fostering it like a colt until it is larger than a mountain.
Allah is good and accepts only good; He told messengers and believers to eat good things, and a traveller's supplication goes unanswered while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful.
Shield yourselves from the Fire even with half a date or a good word; Allah will speak to each without interpreter, who sees only his deeds and the Fire ahead.
Grieved at the poverty of ragged Mudar tribesmen, the Prophet urged charity till heaps formed, saying one who sets a good or evil precedent shares its followers' reward or burden.
When hypocrites mocked a labourer's half sa' gift as unneeded and a larger gift as showing off, a verse was revealed about those who scoff at voluntary givers.
Giving a family a she-camel to milk morning and evening earns a great reward, a reward for each morning and evening drink.
The Prophet likened the giver and the miser to two men in coats of mail: the giver's expands to cover him wholly, the miser's contracts, each ring gripping its place.
Charity given to an adulteress, a rich man and a thief was accepted, as it might restrain her, teach the rich man to spend, and stop the thief stealing.
An honest trustee giving as told, a wife giving her husband's food without harm, and a slave feeding the poor from his master's meat all share reward with the owner.
Those spending pairs for Allah are called through Paradise's gates, the Prophet hoping Abu Bakr would be called through all; one day Abu Bakr did four deeds that bring Paradise.
The Prophet told Asma' to spend and not count or hoard, lest Allah count and withhold from her, and to give according to her means from what Zubair gave her.
Allah shades seven on the Day with no other shade, among them a just ruler, a youth raised in worship, one devoted to mosques, and a secret giver of charity.
The best charity is given while healthy, close-fisted, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth, not delayed until death, when one says this is for so-and-so though it already is theirs.
The giving upper hand is better than the begging lower hand; the best charity leaves the giver self-sufficient and begins with dependents; greedily taken wealth, Hakim was told, is unblessed.
The Prophet said he is only a distributor, Allah the Bestower, and what is begged insistently from him is unblessed; the truly poor are needy yet do not beg.
Constant beggars meet Allah with fleshless faces; selling firewood is better than begging, allowed only for debt, calamity or attested poverty; some companions pledged never to beg.
Umar, and then his collector Ibn al-Sa'di, were told to accept what comes unasked and without greed, even pay for collecting Zakat, but not to long for other wealth.
An old heart stays young in loving wealth and long life; given two valleys of riches, man wants a third, only dust fills him, and Allah turns to the repentant.
True richness is of the soul; the Prophet feared the world's adornment, likening wealth to spring growth, a help when taken rightly; refraining from begging, contentment and endurance are praised.
The Prophet gave even to importunate beggars, saying he was no miser, smiled at a bedouin who pulled his mantle hard and gave him, and kept a cloak for Makhrama.
Sa'd pleaded for a man he called a believer; the Prophet said perhaps a Muslim, and that he gives to some over dearer people lest they fall into the Fire.
The Prophet gave Hunayn's spoils to Quraysh and new Muslims; the Ansar, who answered his call when others fled, complained; he asked if returning with him did not please them.
At Hunayn the Prophet gave chiefs a hundred camels each, completing Abbas b. Mirdas's share, reminded the Ansar of Allah's favours through him, and recalled Moses' patience when called unjust.
Sparing men who called his distribution unjust, the Prophet foretold people whose Quran recital never passes their throats, who pass through religion like an arrow, killed by those nearer truth.
Ali reported the Prophet's order to kill those whose recital does not pass their throats, fought the Khawarij, and found among their dead the man with a defective hand foretold.
Charity is not lawful for the Prophet and his family: he made Hasan drop a charity date, discarded dates that might be charity, and refused to make relatives Zakat collectors.
Charity given to Barira, or to Juwayriya's freed maid, became lawful for the Prophet's household: it was charity for her and a gift for them, having reached its destination.
Sadaqa mutton sent to Umm Atiyya and passed to Aisha had reached its proper place, and the Prophet ate what came as a gift but not as sadaqa.
The Prophet asked Allah to bless those who brought him sadaqa, Abu Aufa's family among them, and the Zakat collector should leave pleased with those he collects from.
When Ramadan comes the gates of mercy are opened, the gates of Hell are locked and the devils are chained.
Do not begin or end the Ramadan fast until the new moon is seen, and if it is cloudy, calculate thirty days; the month may also have twenty-nine.
Showing ten, ten and nine with his fingers, the Prophet taught that a month may be twenty-nine days, adding that his people are unlettered, neither writing nor counting.
Begin the fast on sighting the new moon and end it on sighting the next, and if clouds hide it, complete thirty days.
Do not fast a day or two ahead of Ramadan, unless it is a day on which one already habitually fasts.
Having sworn to stay away from his wives for a month, the Prophet returned after twenty-nine days, saying a month may be twenty-nine, as he showed with his fingers.
Ibn Abbas kept to Medina's sighting rather than Syria's, saying the month counts from when the moon is seen; the months of Eid, Ramadan and Dhu'l-Hijja, are not incomplete.
Some took the verse on the white and black streak to mean threads, until 'from the dawn' was revealed; the Prophet told Adi it means night's blackness and dawn's whiteness.
Bilal's call comes at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum's call, and do not mistake the vertical whiteness for dawn, which spreads across the horizon.
Eating shortly before dawn brings blessing and distinguishes Muslims' fasting from that of the People of the Book; the Prophet's pre-dawn meal ended about fifty verses' time before prayer.
People prosper while they hasten to break the fast, as the Prophet did, breaking it once the sun sets and night comes from the east, even on a journey.
The Prophet forbade uninterrupted fasting, being unlike them as his Lord fed him and gave him drink, and said he would have prolonged it to deter those who persisted.
Aisha reported that the Prophet kissed and embraced his wives while fasting, adding that none controlled his desire as he did.
Aisha, Hafsa and Umm Salama reported the Prophet kissing while fasting; when the questioner said Allah had forgiven his sins, he replied he was the most God-conscious of them.
Aisha and Umm Salama said the Prophet sometimes woke junub from intercourse at dawn and still fasted, and Abu Huraira withdrew his contrary view, which he had from Fadl.
A man who had intercourse by day in Ramadan was told to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor; having nothing, he received food for his family.
In Ramadan of the year of Victory the Prophet set out for Mecca fasting, then drank publicly and broke the fast, calling those who kept fasting disobedient.
Seeing a crowd shading a man who was fasting on a journey, the Prophet said it is no righteousness to fast on a journey, and to take Allah's concession.
Travelling in Ramadan, some companions fasted and some did not, without blame; those not fasting did the work and took the reward, and facing the enemy all broke it.
Hamza al-Aslami was told he may fast on a journey or not, the concession being from Allah, and on a hot journey only the Prophet and Abdullah b. Rawaha fasted.
When people disputed whether the Prophet was fasting on the day of Arafa, Umm al-Fadl, or Maimuna, sent him a cup of milk and he drank it at Arafa.
Quraysh fasted Ashura before Islam and the Prophet commanded it, but once fasting Ramadan became obligatory, he left Ashura optional, calling it one of the days of Allah.
Ibn Mas'ud ate on Ashura, its fast having been left once Ramadan became obligatory, and Mu'awiya quoted the Prophet: Allah did not make it obligatory, though he himself was fasting.
Finding the Jews fasting Ashura for Moses' deliverance from Pharaoh, and treating it as a festival, the Prophet said Muslims are closer to Moses and ordered it fasted.
Ibn Abbas taught fasting the ninth of Muharram; told Jews and Christians revere Ashura, the Prophet said he would fast the ninth next year, but died first.
On Ashura the Prophet had it announced that even those who had eaten should fast the rest of the day, and fasting children were given woollen toys.
The Prophet forbade fasting on the two days of Eid, Fitr and Adha; Ibn Umar, asked about a vow falling on one, cited this ban beside the duty of vows.
The days of Tashriq, the days of Mina, are days of eating, drinking and remembering Allah, and it was announced then that none but a believer enters Paradise.
The Prophet forbade singling out Friday for fasting unless joined to the day before and after or a habitual fast, and singling out its night for prayer.
The verse letting those able to fast feed a needy person instead was abrogated by the verse that whoever witnesses the month must fast it.
Aisha could make up the Ramadan fasts she missed only in Sha'ban, because of her duties to the Prophet.
The heir fasts what a dead person owed, Allah's debt being most deserving of payment, and a woman was told to fast and perform Hajj for her dead mother.
One fasting replies 'I am fasting' to invitations or insults; Allah Himself rewards fasting, a shield, prizing the faster's breath above musk, and Paradise's gate Rayyan admits only fasters.
Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah, Allah removes his face seventy years' distance from Hell.
Finding no food the Prophet would fast, yet ate a gift of hais though he had fasted since morning, and one who eats forgetfully while fasting should complete the fast.
Apart from Ramadan the Prophet never fasted a whole month, at times fasting or not fasting so long people thought he would never change, and fasted most in Sha'ban.
Abdullah b. Amr, fasting daily and praying all night, was told to fast three days monthly or at most David's alternate days, the best fast, and recite the Quran weekly.
Three days monthly with Ramadan is perpetual fasting, alternate days are David's fast, Arafa and Ashura fasts expiate sins, and a missed mid-month fast is made up with two days.
The best fast after Ramadan is in Allah's month al-Muharram, the best prayer after the obligatory is at night, and Ramadan with six Shawwal fasts is like perpetual fasting.
Seeing companions' dreams agree, the Prophet said to seek Lailat-ul-Qadr in the last seven or ten nights of Ramadan, the odd ones, and said he was shown it but forgot.
Seeking Lailat-ul-Qadr in i'tikaf, the Prophet was told it lay in the last ten odd nights and saw himself prostrating in water and clay, which rain left on his forehead.
Seek Lailat-ul-Qadr in the last ten nights; Ubayy b. Ka'b swore it is the twenty-seventh, with a rayless sunrise, and the Prophet mentioned a moon like a piece of plate.
The Prophet kept i'tikaf in Ramadan's last ten days until his death, his wives after him, and once, seeing his wives' tents, struck his own and moved it to Shawwal.
In the last ten nights the Prophet stayed awake, woke his family and exerted himself in devotion more than at any other time.
Aisha never saw the Prophet fasting in the ten days of Dhu'l-Hijja.
One in ihram may not wear a shirt, turban, trousers, cap or saffron-dyed cloth, but one without a lower garment or shoes may wear trousers or trimmed socks.
At Ji'rana, after revelation came upon him, the Prophet told a man in ihram for Umrah to wash off his perfume, remove his cloak and do as in Hajj.
The Prophet fixed where to enter ihram: Dhu'l-Hulaifa for Medina, Juhfa for Syria, Qarn al-Manazil for Najd, Yalamlam for Yemen, Mecca for Meccans; Jabir's report adds Dhat al-'Irq for Iraq.
The Prophet's Talbiya, 'Here I am at Thy service', affirms Allah has no partner and owns praise, grace and sovereignty; Umar and Ibn Umar added words, polytheists added a partner.
The Prophet, after a night and prayer at Dhu'l-Hulaifa, began Talbiya as his camel stood up by its mosque, not at al-Baida', and Ibn Umar modelled four habits on him.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with her own hand, using the best perfume she could find, before he entered ihram and on leaving it before circling the House.
Aisha pictured perfume and musk glistening in the Prophet's hair parting in ihram, and against Ibn Umar's dislike said she perfumed him, he went round his wives, then entered ihram.
The Prophet returned the wild ass, or game meat, given him while in ihram, telling al-Sa'b b. Jaththama it was refused only because they were in ihram.
Pilgrims in ihram could eat the wild ass Abu Qatada hunted out of ihram, as none of them had pointed or helped, and the Prophet ate some; Talha approved likewise.
Five harmful creatures, the crow, kite, rat, scorpion and voracious dog, may be killed in ihram or within the sanctuary without sin, and one version names the snake.
The Prophet named five creatures a pilgrim in ihram may kill without sin, crow, kite, scorpion, rat and voracious dog, in the Ka'ba's precinct too; one report adds the snake.
Troubled by lice in ihram at Hudaibiya, Ka'b b. Ujra was told to shave, fast three days, feed six needy or sacrifice; the verse revealed for him applies to all.
The Prophet was cupped while in ihram, treated sore eyes in ihram with aloes, and Abu Ayyub showed how the Prophet washed his head in ihram.
A pilgrim in ihram whose camel broke his neck is washed with lote-tree water, shrouded in his two cloths, unperfumed, head and face uncovered, to be raised pronouncing Talbiya.
The ailing Duba'a was told to enter ihram on condition of leaving it where Allah detained her; Asma' bint Umais, having given birth, was told to bathe and enter ihram.
Pilgrims took ihram for Umrah, Hajj or both, the Prophet for Hajj; menstruating Aisha was told to undo her hair, leave Umrah for Hajj, then do Umrah from Tan'im.
Those without sacrificial animals turned Hajj ihram into Umrah, the Prophet angered by their hesitation; Aisha, told her Tawaf sufficed, went with her brother to Tan'im; Safiyya could leave.
Jabir recalls those without sacrificial animals leaving ihram fully until Tarwiya, Aisha's menses, Suraqa told it was forever, and Umar later telling people to separate Hajj from Umrah.
Jabir describes the Prophet's Hajj in the tenth year step by step: ihram, Tawaf and Sa'i, Umrah joined to Hajj, the Arafat sermon, Muzdalifa, stoning, sacrifice and Zamzam.
The Hums of Quraish stayed at Muzdalifa while other Arabs went to Arafat, circling the House naked unless clothed by the Hums, until a verse sent everyone to Arafat.
Abu Musa left ihram after Tawaf and Sa'i, as told, and gave verdicts so until Umar, citing the Book and Sunnah, held otherwise, disliking pilgrims enjoying their wives before Hajj.
Uthman forbade Tamattu but Ali practised it; Abu Dharr called it, with temporary marriage, a concession for the Companions alone; Sa'd did it when Mu'awiya was still an unbeliever.
Imran b. Husain taught that the Prophet combined Hajj and Umrah, performing Tamattu; no verse abrogated it, he never forbade it, and one man's contrary view was personal opinion.
Ibn Umar describes the Prophet's Tamattu in the Farewell Pilgrimage; asked by Hafsa why he kept ihram, the Prophet said he had matted his hair and driven his sacrificial animal.
During Hajjaj's attack on Ibn Zubair, Ibn Umar bound himself to Umrah and Hajj together with one Tawaf for both; he and Anas differ on whether the Prophet combined them.
Ibn Umar lets one in Hajj ihram circle the House before Arafat, as the Prophet did; Urwa says the Prophet and those after him began Hajj with Tawaf, keeping ihram.
Asma left ihram having no sacrificial animal while Zubair kept his; she, Aisha and Zubair did Umrah then Hajj, and she confirms the Prophet permitted Tamattu, which Ibn Zubair forbade.
Pre-Islamic Arabs held Umrah in Hajj months a grave sin; the Prophet had those without animals turn Hajj ihram into Umrah, joined to Hajj forever, and a dream approved Tamattu.
At Dhu'l-Hulaifa the Prophet prayed Zuhr, marked his she-camel on the right of its hump, hung two sandals on its neck, then rode to al-Baida' and pronounced Talbiya.
Ibn Abbas held, as the Prophet's Sunnah and from verse 22:33, that circling the House frees a pilgrim from ihram; Mu'awiya says he clipped the Prophet's hair at al-Marwa.
Abu Sa'id recalls Hajj ihram changed to Umrah; Jabir says Umar forbade both Mut'as; Anas reports Ali's ihram matching the Prophet's and heard his Talbiya for Umrah and Hajj together.
The Prophet swore that the son of Mary will pronounce Talbiya for Hajj, Umrah or both in the valley of Rauha.
The Prophet performed four Umrahs, all in Dhu'l-Qa'da but the one with his Hajj, and one Hajj after migrating; Aisha denied Ibn Umar's saying that one was in Rajab.
