Ibn Abbas also said the Prophet stayed fifteen years in Mecca, first hearing Gabriel's voice and seeing his light for seven years, then ten in Medina, and died at sixty-five.
The Prophet named himself Muhammad, Ahmad, al-Mahi through whom unbelief is wiped out, al-Hashir at whose feet people are gathered, al-Aqib after whom no prophet comes, and Prophet of Mercy.
The Prophet was angered when people avoided what he permitted, saying he knew and feared Allah most, and his face changed when an Ansari challenged his water ruling for Zubair.
The Prophet said to avoid what he forbade, since excessive questioning ruined earlier nations and caused prohibitions, and when people pressed him with questions, a verse forbade such asking.
When date-palms bore less after people stopped grafting on his remark, the Prophet said to accept his commands in religion, but his worldly opinion was only a human's.
The Prophet said a day would come when a glimpse of him would be dearer to a person than family, property and everything else.
The Prophet said he is the closest of mankind to Jesus son of Mary, with no prophet between them, and that prophets are brothers of different mothers with one religion.
The Prophet said Satan pricks every newborn, making it cry, except Mary and her son, and Abu Huraira recited the verse seeking protection for her and her offspring from Satan.
Jesus saw a man stealing, and when the man swore by Allah that he had not, Jesus said he believed in Allah and that his own self had deceived him.
Called best of creation, the Prophet said that is Abraham, who circumcised himself at eighty and told only three lies, one protecting Sara from a tyrant who gave her Hajar.
A stone ran off with Moses's clothes while he bathed, showing Banu Isra'il he had no defect; he struck the Angel of Death, then chose death near the sacred land.
A Muslim struck a Jew for swearing by Him who chose Moses; the Prophet forbade ranking prophets, saying when he recovered from the swoon Moses would be holding the Throne.
The Prophet said that on the Night Journey he passed by Moses near the red mound, praying in his grave.
The Prophet said, once quoting Allah, that no servant should say he is better than Yunus son of Matta.
Asked who is most honourable, the Prophet said the most God-fearing, then Joseph, prophet son of prophets, and among Arabs those best before Islam are best in it with understanding.
The Prophet said Zechariah was a carpenter.
Ubayy b. Ka'b reported the Prophet's account of Moses seeking Khadir, more learned than he, by following a lost fish, and of the boat, the boy and the wall.
In the cave the Prophet told a fearful Abu Bakr Allah was their third, and said he would choose Abu Bakr were he to take a bosom friend.
The Prophet named Abu Bakr dearest of men, pointed to him as successor, praised his deeds, and said he and Umar believed in a speaking ox and wolf.
Ali praised Umar at his bier; the Prophet dreamt of Umar's trailing shirt as faith, of milk he passed Umar as knowledge, and of Umar drawing water strongly.
The Prophet saw Umar's palace in Paradise, said Satan shuns him and he would be among the inspired; Allah agreed with Umar thrice, who also opposed praying over Ibn Ubayy.
The Prophet, at ease when Abu Bakr and Umar entered, covered himself for Uthman, saying the angels are modest before him and that he might otherwise not state his need.
At a garden well the Prophet had Abu Musa admit Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman with glad tidings of Paradise, Uthman's coming with a trial he would face.
The Prophet told Ali he was to him as Aaron to Moses, without prophethood after him, and at Khaybar gave him the standard as one loving and loved by Allah.
At Khumm the Prophet said he left the Book of Allah, to hold fast to, and his household, whom Zaid b. Arqam defined as kin forbidden to take Zakat.
Ordered to abuse Ali, Sahl b. Sa'd told how the Prophet found Ali asleep in the mosque covered in dust and called him Abu Turab, the name Ali loved most.
Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas guarded the Prophet at night, was offered the Prophet's parents as ransom at Uhud, had verses revealed about him, and with Talha stayed by the Prophet.
At the Battle of the Trench the Prophet called Zubair his helper, as every prophet has one, and offered him his father and mother as ransom.
When Hira stirred, the Prophet told it only a prophet, a truthful one and a martyr were on it; Aisha said Abu Bakr and Zubair answered Allah's call after misfortune.
The Prophet called Abu Ubaida b. Jarrah this Umma's man of trust, before Yemenis seeking a teacher, and sent him to Najran's people, who asked for a trustworthy man.
The Prophet asked Allah to love Hasan and those who love him, carried Hasan and Husain, and wrapped them, Fatima and Ali in his cloak, reciting the household purification verse.
Zaid b. Haritha was called son of Muhammad until a verse said to name people after their fathers; the Prophet defended Usama's and Zaid's command, both among his dearest.
Abdullah b. Ja'far recalled the Prophet mounting him and Fatima's sons on his beast on returning from journeys, and telling him a secret he would tell no one.
The Prophet said the best women of their time were Mary and Khadija, the perfect women Mary and Asiya, and that Aisha excels women as tharid excels other foods.
Khadija got her Lord's greeting through Gabriel and news of a jewelled palace in Paradise; Aisha was jealous as the Prophet praised her and sent meat to her friends.
The Prophet dreamt of Aisha brought in silk, knew her moods by her oaths, let her play with dolls, and told Fatima, sent by his wives, that he loved Aisha.
In his last illness the Prophet awaited Aisha's turn and died against her chest, asking pardon and mercy and choosing the highest companions, as every prophet is given a choice.
Aisha, jealous when Hafsa swapped camels, excels women like tharid among foods; Gabriel greeted her, and the Prophet said he was to her as Abu Zar' to Umm Zar'.
The Prophet said Fatima is part of him, objecting to Ali also marrying Abu Jahl's daughter, and in his last illness secretly told her of his death and her rank.
Umm Salama took Gabriel, talking with the Prophet, for Dihya; the Prophet said the longest-handed wife would join him first, and it was Zainab, who worked and gave in charity.
The Prophet visited Umm Aiman, who was annoyed when he declined her drink; after his death Abu Bakr and Umar visited her and wept with her that revelation had ceased.
The Prophet visited Umm Sulaim, whose brother was killed with him; he heard her and Bilal's steps in Paradise and blessed her and Abu Talha after their son's death.
The Prophet counted Ibn Mas'ud among the believers of verse 5:93; Abu Musa took him for one of the Prophet's household, and Abu Mas'ud knew no one left more learned.
Ibn Mas'ud recited seventy-plus surahs before the Prophet, who named him, Salim, Ubayy and Mu'adh as Quran teachers; four Ansar collected it, and Allah ordered it recited to Ubayy.
The Prophet said the Throne of the Most Compassionate shook at Sa'd b. Mu'adh's death, and that his kerchiefs in Paradise were better than a silk garment people admired.
At Uhud the Prophet offered his sword to one who would fulfil its right; Abu Dujana took it and struck the heads of the polytheists.
The Prophet said angels shaded Jabir's mutilated father, killed at Uhud, as his relatives wept, and he lifted Julaibib, killed after killing seven, in his arms for burial.
Abu Dharr came to Mecca to find the Prophet, lived on Zamzam water, embraced Islam, proclaimed it aloud and was beaten, and half of his tribe Ghifar then accepted Islam.
Since Jarir embraced Islam the Prophet never refused to see him and always smiled at him, and prayed that he be firm on horseback and rightly guided.
At the Prophet's request Jarir led Ahmas horsemen against Dhu'l-Khalasah, an idol-house called the Yamanite Ka'ba, and destroyed and burned it, and the Prophet blessed Ahmas's horses and men.
Ibn Abbas placed water for the Prophet's ablution, and the Prophet prayed that Allah grant him deep understanding of religion.
Ibn Umar dreamt a silk cloth flew wherever he aimed in Paradise and angels took him to the Fire; the Prophet called him pious and wished he prayed at night.
Umm Sulaim brought Anas to serve the Prophet, who prayed for increase in his wealth and children, and Anas kept a secret the Prophet told him, even from his mother.
The Prophet said Abdullah b. Salam was in Paradise and explained his dream of climbing a pillar to a handhold as holding fast to Islam until death.
The Prophet had Hassan b. Thabit answer the Quraysh's satire for him, with Gabriel's help, and Aisha told a man scolding Hassan to leave him, as he defended the Prophet.
After the Prophet prayed, Abu Huraira's mother accepted Islam; Abu Huraira says he narrates much because he stayed with the Prophet and never forgot, and Aisha faulted his hasty narrating.
Hatib's letter to the Meccans was seized; the Prophet accepted his explanation, refused Umar's wish to kill him as he fought at Badr, and said he would not enter Hell.
The Prophet said none who pledged allegiance under the Tree would enter Hell, and answered Hafsa's objection with the verse that Allah rescues the God-conscious and leaves the tyrants there.
The Prophet gave Abu Musa and Bilal glad tidings a Bedouin refused, prayed forgiveness for Abu Amir and Abu Musa, and praised the Ash'arites' night recitation and food-sharing.
Abu Sufyan asked the Prophet to marry his daughter Umm Habiba, take Mu'awiya as scribe and make him a commander against the unbelievers, and the Prophet agreed to all three.
Asma bint Umais told the Prophet Umar claimed more right to him for emigrating first; he said the people of the boat, back from Abyssinia, had two emigrations, Umar one.
When Abu Bakr rebuked Salman, Suhaib and Bilal for their words about Abu Sufyan, the Prophet said annoying them would annoy his Lord, and Abu Bakr apologised to them.
A verse came down about two Ansar clans, the Prophet prayed for forgiveness for the Ansar and their offspring, and said they were dearest to him and his trusted ones.
The Prophet ranked the best Ansar clans, with good in all; Sa'd b. Ubada was upset his clan came fourth, and Jarir served Anas as the Ansar served the Prophet.
The Prophet said Allah pardoned the tribe of Ghifar and kept Aslam safe, and in prayer cursed Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and Usayya for disobeying Allah and His Messenger.
The Prophet called the Ansar, Quraysh, Muzaina, Juhaina, Ghifar and Ashja' his friends, and said Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaina and Juhaina are better than Tamim, Amir, Asad and Ghatafan.
Tayyi's alms gladdened the Prophet, he prayed for Daws to be guided rather than cursed, and Abu Huraira heard him call Banu Tamim the bravest in battle.
The Prophet said those good before Islam are good in Islam if they understand it, the best shun authority until it is thrust on them, and the worst are double-faced.
The Prophet said the best camel-riding women are those of Quraysh, kind to children when small and careful of a husband's wealth; he said it when proposing to Umm Hani.
The Prophet established brotherhood between the Quraysh and the Ansar in his house, and said Islam has no alliances except those made for good before it, which it strengthens.
The Prophet said he safeguards his Companions and they his community, and armies will win having among them one who saw him, or saw those who saw him.
The Prophet said the best people are his generation, then the next, then the next, after whom come people who testify unasked, break vows, are untrustworthy and grow fat.
The Prophet said none then living on earth would survive a hundred years, and swore to it when asked about the Hour, whose knowledge he said is with Allah.
The Prophet forbade reviling his Companions, saying others spending gold as much as Uhud would not equal a mudd of theirs, after Khalid b. Walid reviled Abd al-Rahman b. Awf.
The Prophet foretold Uwais of Qaran, kind to his mother and cured of leprosy but a spot, and Umar found him and asked him to seek forgiveness for him.
Foretelling the conquest of Egypt, the Prophet urged good treatment of its people for kinship's sake and leaving when two disputed a brick's space, which Abu Dharr later did.
A man the Prophet sent to an Arab tribe was reviled and beaten, and the Prophet said the people of Oman would neither have reviled nor beaten him.
Ibn Umar praised the dead Abdullah b. Zubair hanging by the road; his mother Asma told Hajjaj he had ruined his own Hereafter and was the foretold murderer of Thaqif.
The Prophet said a man of Persia would reach faith even at the Pleiades, placing his hand on Salman when asked about a verse of Surah al-Jumu'a.
The Prophet said people are like a hundred camels, among which not even one is found fit for riding.
The Prophet named the mother three times as most deserving of good treatment, then the father and nearest relatives, and sent back a man seeking jihad to serve his parents.
Ignoring his mother's calls while praying, Juraij was accused of fathering a child as she had prayed, and the infant, one of three who spoke in the cradle, cleared him.
The Prophet said humbled is one whose parents reach old age yet he does not enter Paradise, and the finest goodness is kindness to one's father's loved ones.
The Prophet said virtue is a kind disposition, and vice is what rankles in the heart and what one dislikes people to know.
Allah joins whoever joins kinship and severs the severer, who will not enter Paradise; joining it widens provision and lengthens life, and kindness to harsh relatives brings Allah's help.
The Prophet forbade hatred, envy and enmity among Muslims and keeping away from a brother for more than three days, the better of the two being the first to greet.
The Prophet forbade suspicion, spying, envy, malice and outbidding, called Muslims brothers whose blood, wealth and honour are inviolable, and said Allah looks at hearts and deeds, not faces.
Every Monday and Thursday Allah forgives every servant who associates nothing with Him, except two who bear rancour against each other, who are held back until they reconcile.
Allah will shade on Resurrection Day those who love each other for Him, and an angel told a man visiting his brother for Allah's sake that Allah loves him.
Visiting the sick keeps one in Paradise's fruit garden until he returns, and on Resurrection Day Allah will reproach man for not visiting, feeding or giving drink to His servants.
The Prophet's own fever was severe, and he said a believer's every hardship, even a thorn's prick, wipes away sins, promising Paradise to a woman with falling sickness who endured.
Allah says He forbade oppression, bids His servants seek guidance, food, clothing and forgiveness from Him, cannot be harmed or benefited by them, and repays their recorded deeds.
Oppression is darkness on Resurrection Day, when the wrongdoer pays victims with his good deeds and even a hornless sheep gets its right; Allah respites the oppressor, then seizes him.
When an emigrant and an Ansari called on their groups, the Prophet condemned cries of ignorance and said to help a brother, wrongdoer or wronged; believers are like one body.
When two people abuse each other, the sin falls on the one who began, as long as the wronged one does not go beyond the limit.
The Prophet said charity does not lessen wealth, Allah raises in honour whoever forgives, and raises in rank whoever humbles himself for Allah's sake.
Backbiting is saying of a brother what he dislikes, and if untrue it is slander; Allah will cover on Resurrection Day the faults of a servant who covers others' faults.
The Prophet spoke kindly even to a man he called bad, and said Allah is kind and loves kindness, which adorns all things, and one denied it is denied good.
The Prophet had a cursed camel unloaded and set loose, said cursers are neither intercessors nor witnesses on Resurrection Day, and that he was sent as mercy, not to curse.
Being human, the Prophet asked Allah that any curse, rebuke or blow he gave a Muslim become purification and nearness to Allah, as he told Aisha and Umm Sulaim.
Sent twice by the Prophet to call Mu'awiya, the boy Ibn Abbas found him eating each time, and the Prophet said, May Allah not fill his belly.
The Prophet said the worst of people is the double-faced one, who comes to some people with one face and to others with another.
One who reconciles people by saying good is not a liar, and Ibn Shihab knew of falsehood being allowed only in war, reconciliation, and words between husband and wife.
The Prophet said truth leads to virtue and Paradise and lying to obscenity and Hell till one is recorded truthful or liar, and defined slander as tale-carrying that divides people.
The strong man controls himself in rage rather than wrestling well, and the Prophet said seeking refuge with Allah from Satan would end an angry man's fit.
When Allah shaped Adam in Paradise, Iblis went round him and, finding him hollow, knew he was created unable to control himself.
The Prophet said whoever fights his brother should avoid striking the face, for Allah created Adam in His image.
Seeing people in Syria held in the sun over revenue or jizya, Hisham b. Hakim quoted the Prophet that Allah will torment those who torment people, and they were freed.
Arrows carried in the mosque or market must be held by their heads so no Muslim is hurt, and angels curse whoever points a weapon at his brother.
A man who removed a thorny branch or harmful tree from a path was forgiven and entered Paradise, and the Prophet told Abu Barza to remove harmful things from paths.
A woman entered Hell because of a cat she tied up until it died, neither feeding nor giving it water nor letting it eat the vermin of the earth.
Allah said glory is His lower garment and majesty His cloak, and He will punish whoever contends with Him for them.
Allah forgave a man whom another swore He would not forgive, cancelling the swearer's deeds, and many a dishevelled man turned from doors would have his oath by Allah fulfilled.
The Prophet said that a man who says people are ruined is himself ruined.
Gabriel urged kindness to neighbours on the Prophet so often he thought they would be made heirs, and he told Abu Dharr to add water to his broth for neighbours.
The Prophet told Abu Dharr not to belittle any good, even meeting a brother cheerfully, and bade his Companions speak up for the needy to earn reward.
Good company is like the musk seller, from whom one gains musk or its scent, and bad company like the blacksmith's bellows, which burns clothes or leaves a foul smell.
A woman divided the single date Aisha gave her between her two daughters, eating none, and the Prophet said whoever raises daughters kindly will have protection from Hell.
A mother split the date she meant to eat between her two daughters, earning Paradise, and whoever raises two girls will be close to the Prophet on Resurrection Day.
Parents whose three, or even two, children die, bearing it hoping for reward, are shielded from the Fire, the Prophet told women and a mother who had buried three.
When Allah loves a servant He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces it in heaven, and he is honoured on earth; Allah's anger spreads the same way.
Souls are gathered troops, the familiar agreeing and the opposed differing, and people are like gold and silver mines, the best before Islam best in it with understanding.
Asked when the Last Hour would come by men whose only preparation was love of Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet said a person will be with those he loves.
Asked about a man who does good and is praised or loved by people for it, the Prophet said it is glad tidings given to a believer in this world.
In the womb, after forty nights or more, an angel writes one's sex, livelihood, deeds, lifespan and fortune unalterably, and destiny may overtake someone a cubit from Paradise or Hell.
Everyone's place in Paradise or Hell is written, the pens having dried; asked why then act, the Prophet said act, for each is eased toward what he was created for.
Moses blamed Adam for bringing people out of Paradise, and Adam prevailed by asking why he blamed him for what Allah had ordained for him before creating him.
Allah set creation's measures fifty thousand years before the heavens and earth, turns all hearts as He wills, and created everything by measure, as revealed when Quraysh disputed about destiny.
Allah has fixed a man's share of adultery: the eye's is the lustful look, the tongue's licentious speech, likewise ears, hands and feet, and the heart yearns.
Every child is born on the fitra, his parents making him a Jew, Christian or Magian; asked about those dying young, the Prophet said Allah knows what they would do.
Asked about polytheists' children, the Prophet said Allah knows what they would do; the youth Khadir killed was a disbeliever by nature, and Allah created Paradise's and Hell's people beforehand.
Umm Habiba prayed to benefit from her husband, father and brother; the Prophet said lifespans and provision are fixed, and metamorphosed people left no offspring, apes and swine predating them.
A strong believer is better and dearer to Allah; seek His help without losing heart, and in trouble do not say 'if only', but that Allah did what He ordained.
Reciting the verse on allegorical verses, the Prophet said to avoid them, angrily said earlier peoples perished disputing over the Book, and bade people recite only while hearts agree.
The Prophet said the most despicable person in Allah's sight is the one who keeps falling into disputes with others.
The Prophet said Muslims would follow the ways of those before them step by step, even into a lizard's hole, and confirmed he meant the Jews and Christians.
The Prophet said three times that those who indulged in hair-splitting were ruined.
Before the Hour knowledge will be taken away, ignorance will prevail, wine will be drunk, adultery, bloodshed and miserliness will spread, and one man will look after fifty women.
Allah removes knowledge by taking the scholars, leaving ignorant leaders who give verdicts without knowledge; Aisha had Urwa ask Abdullah b. Amr again a year later, then accepted it.
Starting a good practice in Islam or calling to righteousness earns the reward of all who follow, and starting an evil practice or calling to error carries their sins.
Allah is as His servant thinks of Him and with him when he remembers Him, drawing nearer as he approaches, and those who remember Allah much have gone ahead.
Allah has ninety-nine names, and whoever memorises or enumerates them will enter Paradise; Allah is Odd and loves odd numbers.
One should supplicate with resolve and conviction, never saying 'forgive me if You wish', for no one can compel Allah and nothing is too great for Him to grant.
None should wish for death over hardship, but may ask to live while life is good and die when death is better; Anas and Khabbab refrained for this reason.
Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him: at death the believer, given glad tidings, loves it, while the disbeliever, told of torment, dislikes it.
Allah is with His servant as he thinks of Him and remembers Him, and draws near him faster than he approaches, rushing to him if he comes walking.
A good deed earns tenfold or more, a bad deed its like or forgiveness, and whoever meets Allah with sins filling the earth, associating none with Him, meets equal pardon.
A sick man had asked to be punished in this world instead of the Hereafter; the Prophet told him to ask for good in both and protection from the Fire.
Roving angels seek out gatherings where Allah is glorified and praised, report their requests to Him, and He forgives them all, even a passer-by who merely sat with them.
The supplication the Prophet made most often asked Allah for good in this world and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire, and Anas included it in all his supplications.
Declaring Allah's oneness, or glorifying and praising Him, a hundred times a day wipes out sins and outweighs other deeds; such words are light on the tongue, dear to Allah.
The Prophet taught a desert Arab words of praise, and taught him and new Muslims to ask Allah for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, protection and provision.
Saying 'Hallowed be Allah' a hundred times records a thousand good deeds and wipes out a thousand sins each day.

Allah relieves whoever relieves a brother's distress, conceals the faults of one who conceals, eases Paradise's path for a seeker of knowledge, and sends tranquillity on gatherings studying the Quran.
Angels surround and mercy covers people sitting to remember Allah, and Gabriel told the Prophet that Allah spoke to the angels of the greatness of Companions sitting so.
The Prophet sought Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day and urged people to repent, and Allah accepts whoever repents before the sun rises from the west.
The Prophet told travellers shouting takbir that they call One All-Hearing and near, and taught that 'No might nor power but Allah' is a treasure of Paradise.
The Prophet taught Abu Bakr a supplication for his prayer, confessing great wrong to himself and asking Allah, the Forgiving and Compassionate, for pardon and mercy.
The Prophet sought refuge from the trials of Hell, the grave, wealth, poverty and the Dajjal, from sloth, cowardice, old age, miserliness and debt, and taught protective words against harm.
Going to bed, one should lie on the right side entrusting oneself to Allah, to die on the fitra if death comes; other bedtime words praise Allah and seek protection.
The Prophet sought refuge from the evil of what he had done and not done, in Allah's power from being led astray, and, setting out on journeys, from the Fire.
The Prophet asked forgiveness, the setting right of his religion, world and Hereafter, guidance, chastity and a purified soul, said evening and morning supplications, and taught Ali to seek guidance.
Four phrases of praise the Prophet said thrice outweighed Juwairiya's morning of devotion, and he taught Fatima, asking for a servant, to say takbir, tasbih and tahmid at bedtime.
Hearing a cock, ask Allah's favour, for it sees angels, and a donkey, seek refuge from Satan; in distress the Prophet affirmed Allah's oneness, Lord of the Throne.
The Prophet said the best words, chosen by Allah for His angels and servants and dearest to Him, are 'Hallowed be Allah and praise is due to Him'.
A Muslim's supplication for his brother in his absence is answered, and the commissioned angel says Amen, may it be for you too.
Allah is pleased with the servant who praises Him when he eats a morsel or takes a drink.
A supplication is answered as long as one does not ask for sin or cutting kinship and does not grow impatient, saying he prayed unanswered and giving up supplication.
The Prophet saw that most entering Paradise were poor, the wealthy held back, and most in the Fire were women, and said women would be a minority in Paradise.
The Prophet sought refuge in Allah from the loss of His blessing, the change of His protection, His sudden wrath and all His displeasure.
The Prophet said he left no trial more harmful to men than women; the world is sweet and green, so avoid women's allurement, which caused the Israelites' first trial.
Three men of earlier peoples, shut in a cave by a rock, invoked Allah by deeds done for Him: serving parents, sparing a cousin, repaying a labourer's grown wages.
Allah is more pleased with His servant's repentance than a traveller who, despairing in a waterless desert, finds his lost camel with its provisions.
Had people not sinned, Allah would have replaced them with people who sin, seek His forgiveness and are forgiven, as Abu Ayyub disclosed near his death.
Hanzala called himself a hypocrite for forgetting Paradise and Hell at home; the Prophet said angels would greet them if their remembrance lasted, but there is a time for each.
Allah's mercy prevails over His wrath; of its hundred parts He sent one to creation and kept ninety-nine for Resurrection, and is kinder to His servants than a mother.
A sinful man had his body burnt and scattered for fear of Allah, who gathered him and forgave him; a report adds a woman sent to Hell over a cat.
A servant who keeps sinning and asking forgiveness is forgiven, knowing his Lord forgives; Allah stretches His Hand night and day for repentance until the sun rises in the west.
None loves praise more than Allah, so He praised Himself, and none is more self-respecting, so He forbade abominations; He loves accepting excuses, so He sent the Book and Messengers.
For a man who kissed a woman a verse was revealed: pray, for good deeds remove misdeeds, for everyone; another seeking a prescribed punishment was pardoned for praying.
A killer of a hundred, a monk among them, died journeying in repentance to a land of pious people, and being nearer it was taken by the angels of mercy.
On Resurrection Day Allah would give each Muslim a Jew or Christian as rescue from Hell, forgiving heavy sins, and pardon a believer's concealed faults while exposing disbelievers and hypocrites.
Ka'b b. Malik recounted staying behind from Tabuk without excuse, telling the truth, being boycotted with two others fifty nights, until Allah revealed He accepted their repentance.
Ka'b b. Malik tells how he stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse, told the Prophet the truth, was shunned fifty nights with two others, until Allah accepted their repentance.
Aisha tells of the false charge against her after she was left behind on a journey, her grief, the Prophet's consultations and address, and the verses revealing her innocence.
A man was charged with fornication with the Prophet's slave girl; told to strike his neck, Ali found the man's sexual organ cut off and refrained.
Revelation confirms Zaid b. Arqam against Abdullah b. Ubayy, whom at death the Prophet shrouds in his shirt and prays over despite Umar, before a verse forbids it.
Three persons by the House disputed whether Allah hears them when they speak loudly or in undertones, and the verse about ears, eyes and skins bearing witness was revealed.
When some turned back on the way to Uhud, the Companions split over killing them, and the verse asking why they were two parties over the hypocrites came down.
Hypocrites stayed behind from the Prophet's battles, then made excuses and oaths wanting praise for what they had not done, and a verse warning of painful chastisement was revealed.
Ibn Abbas told Marwan the verse on loving undeserved praise concerned People of the Book, who hid what the Prophet asked them, told him something else, and rejoiced.
Hudhaifa relates that twelve hypocrites of the Prophet's Ummah will be kept from Paradise, and says twelve of the people of Aqaba were enemies of Allah and His Messenger.
All who climbed the hill of Murar were pardoned except the owner of a red camel, who preferred finding his lost thing to the Prophet seeking forgiveness for him.
A scribe of the Prophet from Banu Najjar ran away to join the People of the Book; after his death the earth threw him out each time they buried him.
A gale blew at a hypocrite's death, two hypocrites face a fiercer fever on Resurrection Day, and a hypocrite is like a sheep straying between two flocks.
A bulky person on the Day of Judgement will not weigh as much as a gnat before Allah, as the verse says no balance will be set up for them.
A Jewish scholar says Allah will hold all creation on His fingers, the Prophet smiling agreement; on Judgement Day Allah will grip earth and heavens, saying: I am the Lord.
The Prophet lists what Allah created on each day of the week, from clay on Saturday to Adam after Asr on Friday, the last creation.
On the Day of Resurrection people gather on a white plain, stand on the Sirat when earth and heaven are changed, and the earth becomes one bread for Paradise's people.
The Prophet says that if ten Jewish scholars followed him, no Jew on earth would remain outside Islam.
When Jews asked the Prophet about the Soul he stayed silent until revelation came that the Soul is by his Lord's command and people are given little knowledge.
Al-As b. Wa'il will not pay Khabbab unless he denies Muhammad, saying he will pay once raised with his property and children, and a verse comes down.
Abu Jahl asks Allah for stones if the Prophet is true, and vows to trample the praying Prophet's neck but recoils from a ditch of fire; verses come down.
Ibn Mas'ud explains the Smoke as what starving Quraysh saw in the famine the Prophet invoked, one of five signs now past; Ubayy lists it among worldly punishments.
In the Prophet's lifetime the moon split in two, one part either side of the mountain at Mina, when Mecca's people asked for a sign, and he said: Bear witness.
None is more patient than Allah at hearing irksome things: people ascribe partners and a son to Him, yet He protects them and provides for them.
On Resurrection Day a disbeliever would give the earth's gold as ransom, though only not associating partners with Allah was asked of him, and disbelievers assemble on their faces.
Dipped once in the Fire, a denizen of Hell who lived in luxury will deny knowing comfort, and dipped once in Paradise, the world's most miserable will deny all hardship.
Allah rewards a believer's good deeds in this world and the Hereafter, while a disbeliever is repaid for his deeds in this world and finds none left in the Hereafter.
A believer is like a crop tossed by wind, a hypocrite or disbeliever like a cypress uprooted at once, and a Muslim like the date-palm, whose leaves do not wither.
Satan despairs of being worshipped in Arabia but sows discord, prizing most whoever splits spouses; everyone has a devil, but Allah keeps the Prophet safe from his.
No one, not even the Prophet, enters Paradise by deeds alone, only through Allah's Mercy, so act moderately, and the deed Allah loves most is the constant one.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, and when told his earlier and later sins were pardoned, he asked whether he should not be a grateful servant.
Ibn Mas'ud preached once a week rather than daily, lest his listeners be bored, as the Prophet left days without sermons for the same reason.
Paradise is surrounded by hardships and the Fire by temptations.
Allah has prepared for His pious servants what no eye saw, no ear heard and no heart perceived, as the verse says no soul knows what is hidden for them.
In Paradise a rider cannot cross a tree's shade in a hundred years, and Allah tells its people He will grant them His pleasure and never be displeased with them.
Paradise's people will see those in the chambers above them like shining planets on the horizon, and believers who affirm the truth will reach the abodes of the Apostles.
The Prophet says those of his Ummah he loves most will come after him, each longing to see him even at the cost of family and wealth.
A street of Paradise visited each Friday adds beauty, and the first to enter have faces like the full moon, no bodily waste, musk sweat, gold combs and two wives.
Paradise's people eat and drink without waste, their food passing as belching and musk sweat; they praise Allah as they breathe and are promised lasting health, life, youth and plenty.
A believer in Paradise has a tent of one hollow pearl sixty miles wide; Saihan, Jaihan, Euphrates and Nile are among its rivers, and some enter with hearts like birds'.
Allah created Adam in His image, sixty cubits tall, and had him greet the angels, whose reply became his offspring's greeting, and all who enter Paradise will have his form.
Hell is dragged by seventy thousand bridles, earthly fire is a seventieth of it, a stone fell seventy years to its floor, and fire reaches people from ankles to collar-bones.
Hell claims the proud and Paradise the humble in their dispute; Allah calls them His punishment and His mercy, fills Hell by placing His foot, and creates others for Paradise.
Death, brought as a white ram, is slaughtered between Paradise and Hell, and both peoples are told they will live forever without death, to one's delight and the other's grief.
In Hell a disbeliever's molar will be like Uhud, his skin three nights' journey thick, and the span of his shoulders a swift rider's three-day journey.
Paradise's people are the meek and humble, whose oaths Allah fulfils even when they are driven from doors, and Hell's people are the haughty and proud.
In a sermon the Prophet recites the verse on the man who hamstrung the dromedary, then warns against flogging one's wife like a slave and laughing at breaking wind.
The Prophet saw Amr, named b. Luhayy or b. Amir, the first to devote animals to idols, dragging his intestines in the Fire; Ibn Musayyib explains the bahira and sa'iba.
Among Hell's people are those with whips like ox tails who flog people, living under Allah's wrath, and women clothed yet naked, misled and misleading, who will not smell Paradise.
Compared with the Hereafter, this world is like what clings to a finger dipped in the ocean.
People will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, too troubled to look at one another; Abraham is clothed first, and some of the Prophet's companions are taken to the left.
People will be gathered in three groups, and with the sun a mile away they will stand in sweat according to deeds, up to knees, waists, mouths or ears.
The Prophet relays that Allah made His servants inclined to worship until Satan misled them, ordered him to fight Quraysh, and named three kinds in Paradise, five in Hell.
The dead are shown their seat morning and evening, the Prophet hears graves' torment, two angels question the buried, and two angels carry a believer's soul up.
The Prophet showed where each of Badr's dead would fall, then called to the Quraysh dead in the well, telling Umar they heard him but could not reply.
Whoever is thoroughly examined in the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is ruined; the easy reckoning in the verse is only the presentation of deeds.
Three days before his death the Prophet said that none should die except hoping only good from Allah.
Every servant will be raised in the state in which he dies, and when Allah punishes a people all are struck, then raised according to their deeds.
The Prophet warned of ruin for Arabia and that Gog and Magog's barrier had opened this much, saying people perish though good ones are among them when evil prevails.
An army sent against those seeking refuge at the House will sink into the earth on a plain, and those forced along will be raised by their intentions.
The Prophet saw turmoil falling among Medina's houses like rain; in coming turmoil sitting beats standing, so seek shelter, keep to one's flock or land, and blunt one's sword.
Two Muslims meeting with swords are both in the Fire; much bloodshed will precede the Hour, and Allah withheld the Prophet's request that his Ummah be spared killing one another.
Hudhaifa says the Prophet once described every turmoil to come before the Last Hour, some remembering and some forgetting, and Abu Zaid recalls a dawn-to-sunset address on past and future.
Hudhaifa tells Umar that a door, Umar himself, stands between him and the turmoil surging like waves and will be broken, and Jundub disputes with Hudhaifa over bloodshed at Jara'a.
Before the Hour the Euphrates will bare a gold mountain over which ninety-nine in a hundred die fighting, so take none; Iraq, Syria and Egypt will withhold coins and measures.
Before the Hour Romans will fight an army from Medina at Dabiq, whose victors take Constantinople before Jesus descends against the Dajjal, and the Romans will be the majority.
Before the Hour a war with Rome kills so many that spoils bring no joy, then news of the Dajjal comes; Arabia, Persia, Rome and the Dajjal will be conquered.
Ten signs precede the Hour: the smoke, the Dajjal, the beast, the sun rising in the west, Jesus's descent, Gog and Magog, three landslides and a fire driving people.
Before the Hour a fire from Hijaz will light camels' necks at Busra, Medina's dwellings will reach Ihab, and famine will come despite heavy rain as nothing grows.
Facing the east, the Prophet said turmoil would appear from there, where the horns of Satan rise; Salim reproached Iraqis for asking about minor sins while committing major ones.
Before the Hour, Daus women will circle Dhi al-Khalasa and Lat and Uzza be worshipped; a fragrant wind will take all with faith, the rest reverting to their forefathers' religion.
A man passing a grave will wish to be in it from calamity, and amid general bloodshed killer and slain will not know why, both in the Fire.
An Abyssinian with two small shanks will destroy the Ka'ba; before the Hour a man of Qahtan will drive people with his stick, and al-Jahjah will take the throne.
Before the Hour Muslims will fight peoples wearing hair shoes, with faces like hammered shields, small eyes, snub noses and red complexions, named in one report as the Turks.
Jabir said non-Arabs and Romans may stop Iraq's and Syria's food and money, and the Prophet said a caliph of the last age will give out wealth uncounted.
The Prophet told Ammar, digging the ditch, that rebels would kill him, and said this Quraish tribe would kill people of his Ummah, who had best keep apart from them.
Kisra and Caesar will die with no Kisra or Caesar after them, and the believers will spend their treasures in the cause of Allah.
These entries have no text in the source; they are kept with the report before them that Kisra and Caesar will die and their treasures be spent for Allah.
The Prophet tested Ibn Sayyad and kept Umar from killing him; Ibn Sayyad argued he was not the Dajjal, Paradise's earth was likened to musk, and Umar swore he was.
The Prophet tried to overhear Ibn Sayyad and warned the Dajjal is one-eyed, unlike Allah, with Kafir between his eyes; Hafsa told Ibn Umar anger would bring the Dajjal out.
Allah is not one-eyed, but the Dajjal is blind in the right eye, like a floating grape; every prophet warned of him, and Kafir is written between his eyes.
The Dajjal brings water and fire, or Paradise and Hell, each really the other, so whoever meets him should drink from what looks like fire; Noah too warned of him.
The Dajjal commands rain and treasures until Jesus kills him at Ludd; Gog and Magog swarm and perish, the earth is blessed, and a wind takes every Muslim.
The Dajjal kills and revives a believer who exposes him but cannot kill him again; the Prophet told Mughira he is insignificant to Allah despite his food and water.
Jesus kills the Dajjal; after seven peaceful years a cold wind takes all with faith, Satan leads the wicked to idols, and the trumpets raise people for judgement.
Abdullah b. Amr remembered that the first signs are the sun rising in the west and the beast appearing in the forenoon, the second following soon after the first.
From the pulpit the Prophet retold Tamim Dari's account of the chained Dajjal on an island, who would roam every land but Mecca and Medina, confirming his own words.
The Dajjal will cover every land but Mecca and Medina, whose passes angels guard; Medina will shake out its disbelievers and hypocrites, and seventy thousand Jews of Isfahan follow him.
People will flee from the Dajjal to the mountains, when the Arabs will be few, and no creation from Adam to the Hour is a greater trouble than he.
Hasten to good deeds before six things: the sun rising in the west, the smoke, the Dajjal, the beast, death and turmoil; worship amid turmoil is like emigrating to the Prophet.
The Hour will befall the wicked; the Prophet and it were sent like joined fingers; a boy present would not grow old before it came to them; it comes suddenly.
Forty separate the two trumpet blasts; then rain falls and people sprout like plants, rebuilt from the tailbone, the one bone the earth does not consume.
The world is the believer's prison and the unbeliever's paradise; showing a dead lamb no one wanted, the Prophet said the world is worth even less to Allah.
The son of Adam says 'my wealth', yet only what he eats, wears out or gives in charity is his; family, wealth and deeds follow his bier, only deeds staying.
The Prophet feared for them not poverty but riches they would vie over to their ruin, as earlier peoples did, and foretold rivalry and enmity once Persia and Rome fell.
Look at those below you in wealth and form, not at those above you, so that you do not belittle Allah's favours to you.
Allah tested a leper, a bald man and a blind man of Bani Isra'il with cures and herds; begged by the angel, only the blind man gave, pleasing Allah.
Rebuked by his son for tending camels while others fought over rule, Sa'd cited the Prophet: Allah loves the servant who is God-conscious, free from want and hidden.
Sa'd, the first Arab to shoot an arrow in Allah's cause, recalled having only tree leaves to eat with the Prophet, and protested that Banu Asad instructed him in religion.
Utba b. Ghazwan preached that the world is ending, Hell is deep and Paradise vast, recalling eating leaves with the Prophet, and warned that prophethood gives way to kingship.
Believers will see their Lord as clearly as sun and moon; Allah will question servants who forgot meeting Him, and a hypocrite's mouth is sealed while his limbs testify.
The Prophet asked Allah to give Muhammad's family bare sustenance, and Aisha said his family never ate their fill of wheat bread three days running until he died.
These entries have no text in the source; they are kept with Aisha's reports before them that the Prophet's family seldom ate their fill.
At al-Hijr, Thamud's dwellings, the Prophet said to enter only weeping, hurried through, and had its well water spilt and water taken from the she-camel's well.
Whoever works for a widow and the destitute is like one striving in Allah's cause, or like one who constantly stands in prayer and fasts without break.
Whoever looks after an orphan, related or not, will be with the Prophet in Paradise like two fingers held together.
When people objected to Uthman rebuilding the Prophet's mosque, he cited the Prophet: whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah builds him a house in Paradise.
A voice ordered a cloud to water a man's garden; he gave a third of its yield in charity, ate a third with his family and put a third back.
Allah says He needs no partner: whoever does a deed associating another with Him, He leaves him with that partner.
Whoever seeks to publicise his deeds, Allah will publicise him, and whoever makes a show of them, Allah will make a show of him.
A servant may speak words, not weighing their consequence, that sink him into the Fire farther than the distance between east and west.
Usama said he had spoken to Uthman and would not flatter a ruler, citing a man in Hell circling his spilled intestines who enjoined good but did not practise it.
All of the Prophet's Ummah will be pardoned except those who expose their sins, telling people by day what they did at night under Allah's cover.
Only a sneezer who praises Allah is answered with 'May Allah have mercy on you', not a second sneeze from a cold; yawning is from Satan and should be restrained.
Angels were created from light, jinn from a spark of fire, and Adam as he has been described to you.
A lost group of Bani Isra'il was perhaps turned into rats, which drink goat's milk but not camel's; Ka'b repeatedly asked Abu Huraira if the Prophet said it.
A believer is not stung twice from the same hole, and every affair of a believer is good: he thanks Allah in joy and is patient in hardship.
The Prophet said over-praising a man breaks his neck, so say only 'I think him so', not declaring anyone pure before Allah, and throw dust in flatterers' faces.
In a vision, as the Prophet used a miswak, two men vied for it; he gave it to the younger but was told to give it to the elder.
Aisha said the Prophet spoke so distinctly his words could be counted; he said to write nothing from him but the Quran, yet narrate from him, never lying about him.
A boy taught by a king's magician followed a monk, healed through Allah, and could be killed only in Allah's name; believers in his Lord were cast into fiery ditches.
Abu Yasar wrote off a debt and urged clothing servants as oneself; Jabir recalled rules on spitting, cursing and prayer rows, trees obeying the Prophet and water from his fingers.
Abu Bakr told how, travelling by night with the Prophet, he got him milk from a shepherd, Suraqa's mount sank when the Prophet cursed him, and Medina welcomed the Prophet.
Told to enter saying Hitta, asking forgiveness, the people of Israel entered dragging themselves on their buttocks and twisted the word into 'a grain in the ear'.
Allah sent revelation to the Prophet in quick succession before his death, and on the day he died it came most abundantly.
A Jew told Umar that had 'This day I have perfected your religion' come to them, they would celebrate its day; Umar said it came at Arafat on a Friday.
Aisha said the verses on orphan girls bar guardians from marrying them for their wealth without a fair dowry or keeping them unmarried, and let a poor guardian eat reasonably.
Aisha said the verse 'When they came upon you from above you and from below you' concerns the day of the Ditch.
Aisha said the verse on a wife fearing her husband's aversion concerns a long-married wife he would divorce, who asks him to keep her, permitting him another wife.
Aisha told Urwa that Muslims were commanded to ask forgiveness for the Prophet's companions, but they reviled them instead.
Ibn Abbas held that the verse giving Hell to whoever kills a believer intentionally was never abrogated, the Furqan verse offering repentance being Meccan and about polytheists.
Ibn Abbas confirmed that 'When came the help from Allah and the victory' was the last sura revealed as a whole.
After Muslims killed a man who greeted them with peace and took his sheep, the verse came: do not tell one who greets you that he is not a Muslim.
When the Ansar on pilgrimage entered their houses only from the back, the verse 'Piety is not that you come to the doors from behind' was revealed.
Ibn Mas'ud said four years passed between their acceptance of Islam and the verse asking whether believers' hearts should not humble for Allah's remembrance.
Before Islam women circled the Ka'ba naked, asking for a cloth to cover them, and the verse 'Adorn yourself at every place of worship' was revealed.
Abdullah b. Ubayy b. Salul forced his slave-girls Musaika and Umaima into prostitution; they complained to the Prophet, and the verse forbidding compelling slave-girls to prostitution was revealed.
Ibn Mas'ud said 'Those whom they call upon themselves seek access to their Lord' concerns jinn who became Muslims while the people worshipping them kept on.
Ibn Abbas said Sura Tauba kept naming people with 'of them' until none seemed spared, Sura Anfal concerns Badr, and Sura al-Hashr concerns Banu Nadir.
Umar said wine, when forbidden, was made from grape, date, honey, wheat and barley, and is whatever clouds the mind, wishing for more detail on inheritance and interest.
Abu Dharr swore that 'These two adversaries who dispute about their Lord' concerns Hamza, Ali and Ubaida, who came out at Badr against Utba, Shaiba and Walid.
